title: Kyle Whittingham buyout: Cost of firing Michigan football coach after failed year
content:
It’s been a rough start to the Kyle Whittingham era for Michigan football, which has led many to call for the program to pull the plug after the 2026 college football season.

Michigan needed a phantom second to win the season opener on a Hail Mary over Western Michigan, and things have snowballed ever since. Add in a loss to rival Michigan State and an embarrassing effort against the Oregon Ducks in Week 11, and many are calling for Whittingham to be fired.

But at what cost?

As is the case with many high-profile college football coaches, the buyout is part of the conversation. If the Wolverines were to move on from Whittingham after the 2026 season. We have answers.

MORE: Dave Portnoy calls for firing of Michigan’s Kyle Whittingham

Cost of Kyle Whittingham Buyout

Whittingham signed a five-year, $41 million contract in the offseason to replace Sherrone Moore as Wolverines head coach.

Luckily for Michigan, his buyout percentage is just 75 percent, which would allow the team to move on at a cheaper rate than many of its Big Ten rivals.

MORE: When will college football AP Top 25 rankings release for Week 12? Poll delayed after FAA ground stop

If Michigan were to fire Whittingham, it would cost approximately $25 million ($24.75 million).

Add in a new athletic director in 2027 after Warde Manuel steps down, and the Wolverines could have a clear path to move forward. Instead of struggling through another rough season, Michigan could be wise to pull the plug early and start over ahead of the recruiting cycle to attract top players and instill confidence that the 2026 struggles were nothing more than a fluke.

title: Will A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson play today? Injury updates, fantasy advice for Week 10
content:
The New England Patriots have a pair of injury concerns going into the Week 10 game versus the Detroit Lions with wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back Rhamondre Stevenson.

Not only has Brown dealt with injuries in his first year in New England, he also hasn’t been productive when on the field.

After suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 1, Brown returned to action in Week 6, but his return was short-lived because he came down with ankle and knee issues in Week 8 that forced him to miss two more games.

MORE: Bold predictions in fantasy football Week 10

As for Stevenson, he suffered a knee injury in Week 9 that was expected to keep him sidelined for multiple games.

However, both Brown and Stevenson were able to practice this week, with Brown turning in three limited sessions and Stevenson posting two. Both are listed as questionable.

Here’s the latest on their statuses for the contest against the Lions in Munich, Germany.

Will A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson play today?

It appears both Stevenson and Brown are going to overcome their injuries to play on Sunday, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter.

“Patriots WR A.J. Brown and RB Rhamondre Stevenson, both listed as questionable for this morning’s game in Munich Germany, both are expected to play, per sources,” Schefter reported.

Make sure to double check the inactives to confirm. Those will drop around 8 a.m. ET with the kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. ET stateside.

A.J. Brown start-sit-advice

For the first time in his career, there is actually a debate to be had about whether or not to start Brown, who has always been a lineup lock.

In three games with the Pats, Brown hasn’t surpassed more than 48 yards and he has just six catches for 53 yards over his last two contests.

Now, we have the added concern about him possibly being at less than 100%.

MORE: Fantasy football wide receiver rankings for Week 10

But this is just too good of a matchup to sit him for.

The Lions sport the worst pass defense in the NFL and are giving up the 11th-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers, according to CBS Sports.

If Brown doesn’t get going this week, he might be bench fodder moving forward.

Verdict: Start

Rhamondre Stevenson start-or-sit advice

We do have some concern about Stevenson seeing a limited workload because he may not be 100%, but there haven’t been any reports suggesting that as of this writing, so we have to expect he’ll be a full go.

Stevenson’s fantasy production hasn’t been great, but he still ranks as RB21 overall in fantasy points per game, according to Fantasy Pros, which makes him a weekly flex option in all formats.

As bad as they’ve been against the pass, the Lions are stingy against the run, as evidenced by their giving up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs.

MORE: Fantasy football running back rankings for Week 10

But this is a game that could feature a lot of scoring opportunities with two defenses that have seen some struggles. Stevenson also has very little competition for work now that TreVeyon Henderson is on injured reserve.

Volume alone is enough to justify starting Stevenson in a tough matchup.

Verdict: Start

title: College Football game between Louisville and UNC ends in heated on-field brawl
content:
Louisville Cardinals‘ 16-14 victory over North Carolina Tar Heels ended with a heated on-field brawl as players from both college football teams clashed after the final whistle on Saturday night.

The incident happened in Chapel Hill after the Cardinals secured their fifth consecutive win. Players began exchanging words during Louisville’s victory formation before pushing escalated into several physical confrontations.

The tension followed a crucial defensive play by Louisville. With 58 seconds remaining, defensive back Jabari Mack intercepted a fourth-down pass from North Carolina quarterback Travis Burgess.

Mack returned the ball 32 yards before sliding to secure possession. Louisville then ran out the clock to claim the two-point victory.

MORE: Landry Kiffin turns heads in stunning yellow minidress for final LSU home game

However, the postgame celebration soon turned into chaos. North Carolina defensive tackle Xavier Lewis and Louisville offensive lineman Johnnie Brown III continued jostling after the final kneel-down.

Other players soon joined the confrontation. Several pushed and grabbed opponents, while apparent punches were thrown during multiple skirmishes across the field.

We got a brawl at the end of the Louisville vs UNC game pic.twitter.com/nIeyCwJuOc

— gmannVOLS (@gmannVOLS) November 15, 2026

Louisville and UNC coaches react to the brawl

North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick stepped onto the field to help separate players. One confrontation also spilled into the end zone, where another group became involved.

Belichick addressed the incident after the game, making his position clear.

“You play the game between the whistles, that’s not what we’re here for,” Belichick said. “We got out there and got everybody out as quickly as possible.”

Louisville coach Jeff Brohm also expressed disappointment about the incident.

“It’s obviously unfortunate,” Brohm said. “You try to get things broken up as fast as you can. It didn’t get broken up too fast, and you never want to see that happen.

“I’d have to see what really started it. Hopefully we can correct that and not do that again.”

MORE: When will college football AP Top 25 rankings release for Week 12? Poll delayed after FAA ground stop

The Cardinals improved to 7-3 overall and 6-2 in the ACC. North Carolina dropped to 5-5 and remains one victory away from bowl eligibility.

Louisville will host Pittsburgh next Saturday, while North Carolina travels to Virginia. Neither team nor the ACC has announced disciplinary action.

title: Dave Portnoy calls for firing of Michigan’s Kyle Whittingham
content:
Dave Portnoy is not happy with how things are going at Michigan, and the Barstool Sports founder has made his feelings about head coach Kyle Whittingham clear. Portnoy wants the Wolverines to make a coaching change, even if it takes a disastrous end to the season to force the decision.

Portnoy’s latest comments came after Michigan suffered another disappointing defeat, losing 31-7 to No. 16 Oregon on Saturday. The result added to the frustration surrounding Whittingham’s first season in Ann Arbor. Michigan has now lost five of its last seven games after opening the season 3-0.

MORE: Michigan has become biggest disappointment in college football

Dave Portnoy wants Kyle Whittingham gone

Portnoy made it clear that he would rather see Michigan continue losing than watch the head coach remain in charge.

“I want Michigan to lose every game by 1000 the rest of the season so we have no choice but to fire Whittingham,” Portnoy said.

I want Michigan to lose every game by 1000 the rest of the season so we have no choice but to fire Whittingham

— Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) November 14, 2026

Michigan’s struggles have been building for weeks. The Wolverines suffered a 15-6 home defeat to Michigan State on Nov. 7, a result that prompted Portnoy to demand the firing of offensive coordinator Jason Beck.

Michigan fired Beck on Nov. 8, but the coaching change has yet to produce the desired improvement.

Whittingham arrived at Michigan after spending 21 seasons as Utah’s head coach. His appointment initially generated excitement among Wolverines supporters, including Portnoy, who previously described the move as a spectacular hire.

However, his first season has taken a difficult turn, and the pressure on him continues to grow.

Michigan has two regular-season games remaining, including a home matchup against UCLA on Nov. 21 and the rivalry showdown against Ohio State on Nov. 28.

title: Is Amon-Ra St. Brown playing today? Injury update, fantasy advice for Week 10
content:
For the second straight week, Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown‘s status for a game is up in the air.

Ahead of the Week 10 game in Munich, Germany, St. Brown is listed as questionable to play with a rib injury.

As was the case last week, the Lions wide receiver turned in three limited practices in the week leading up to the game before getting the designation.

MORE: Bold predictions in Fantasy Football Week 10

Here’s what we know about St. Brown’s chances of suiting up on Sunday against the New England Patriots.

Is Amon-Ra St. Brown playing today?

While nobody has confirmed St. Brown’s status, history tells us he is going to play against the Patriots on Sunday.

St. Brown has garnered the reputation as one of the toughest players in the NFL during his career because he has played through some injuries most players succumb to.

In fact, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that whenever he reaches out to his source with the Lions to ask if St. Brown is going to play with an injury, he nearly gets laughed at.

MORE: Fantasy Football wide receiver rankings for Week 10

“He’s officially listed as questionable, but I would be surprised if he didn’t play,” Fowler stated. “He always plays. I was talking to people in Detroit. anytime I check on St. Brown they almost laugh it off like, yeah, he’s going to play. He once played on a high-ankle sprain on a Thursday night and balled out, so, that’s the expectation.”

St. Brown has even more motivation to play this week because the game is in Germany, where his family has roots with his mother being born and raised in Leverkusen, Germany.

There is no way St. Brown is sitting out on Sunday.

Amon-Ra St. Brown fantasy advice

You know the drill here: St. Brown is never on the bench, regardless of matchup.

But get excited for the potential he posts absurd production on Sunday.

Not only are the Patriots giving up the most fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season, according to CBS Sports, but St. Brown is going to be extra motivated to produce a memorable showing because the game is in Germany.

St. Brown hasn’t scored a touchdown since Week 3, which is shocking, but we think the Lions will make it a point to get him one in Munich.

title: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel goes viral after beer celebration in Munich
content:
New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel grabbed attention in Munich after joining local fans for a traditional beer celebration ahead of Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions.

A video of Vrabel tapping a beer keg and drinking from a frosted stein at a Munich beer hall went viral on Saturday, Nov. 14. The event took place the night before the Patriots’ Week 10 NFL International Game at Allianz Arena, which raised questions among a section of fans.

Vrabel visited Augustiner Stammhaus, one of Munich’s designated Patriots fan pubs. He stepped behind the bar, used a mallet to tap a wooden beer cask and poured himself a large mug.

MORE: Patriots’ Milton Williams introduces unique punishment for defensive penalty problems

After ringing the bar bell, Vrabel addressed the cheering crowd.

“Listen, I knew we had fans in Germany, I didn’t know we had this many fans. Thank you for your support, go Pats, let’s raise a glass to everybody”.

Coach Vrabel taps the Keg! 🍻 pic.twitter.com/Zw1FoPlFfb

— New England Patriots (@Patriots) November 14, 2026

Some fans reacted to the viral video, with one saying, “If we lose, this is gonna end up looking even worse,” while another said, “We’re getting 30-bombed tomorrow.”

The Patriots coach also spent time with local youth flag football players during an NFL-run clinic on Friday. His visit gave German fans an opportunity to meet the coach before Sunday’s international matchup.

Mike Vrabel looks to turn Patriots’ attention back to football

The celebration comes after a difficult Week 9 result for New England. The Patriots suffered a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers, dropping their record to 5-4.

Vrabel did not hide his frustration after the defeat.

“We lost, and we got our a***s kicked,” Vrabel said. “There’s no two ways around it.”

New England now faces a difficult challenge against the 6-2 Detroit Lions. The Patriots need a strong response before entering their bye week. Quarterback Drake Maye has thrown for 2,282 yards and 18 touchdowns through nine games. However, his 11 interceptions remain a concern for the offense.

MORE: Cowboys make multiple roster moves ahead of Sunday’s 49ers game

Sunday’s matchup offers Vrabel and the Patriots an opportunity to respond after their disappointing performance. The coach’s Munich celebration has attracted attention, but his team must now deliver on the field.

title: College Football Rankings: Texas, Wake Forest Jumped As LSU, USC Fell After Week 11
content: The biggest disappointment in college football is LSU coach Lane Kiffin. And it’s not close. With the loss to Texas on Saturday, Kiffin sealed LSU’s fate and his as the most-overrated and underperforming program the sport has seen since 2019 Oklahoma with one caveat: At least the Sooners made the College Football Playoff. LSU will be lucky to get selected for the Citrus Bowl. Serves it right. LSU made a mess 11 months ago to get Kiffin, who left a team that was assured its first invitation to the CFP to collect a salary that pays him on par with Georgia coach Kirby Smart and Indiana coach Curt Cignetti. He is one of the highest-paid coaches by annual salary in college football. The Tigers administration and donors also wrote a check for Kiffin’s roster that is widely accepted as the richest in the sport. The bare minimum Kiffin was expected to do in Year 1 was make the College Football Playoff. Eleven days before Thanksgiving, LSU crashed out of the CFP conversation with a fourth loss to a ranked opponent and is 3-4 in the SEC standings. It’s an eight-win team at best. That’s what $13 million gets you, LSU — or at least when you give it to Kiffin. But let's get into my latest top-25 rankings. After losses, a bit of travel chaos and several teams winning despite their injured rosters, three teams dropped off my list (SMU, South Carolina and New Mexico) and were replaced by a returner and two making their debuts. And in case you missed it: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights across the country on Friday, and its decision wrecked travel plans for many teams. Start times for some games were pushed back, save one, which was bumped back a whole day. Oklahoma will host Ole Miss at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, and after that game, I will update my rankings as necessary. Week 11 game: 28-23 win vs. Middle TennesseeWeek 12 game: vs. Western Kentucky The Flames' only loss this season came in their opener against James Madison. Along with Boise State, they are the last one-loss team left in the Group of Six. That counts for something. Stat to know: Through Week 11, Liberty boasts a +1.55 net yards per play differential (6.38 yards per play gained vs. 4.83 yards per play allowed), which ranks 13th in the FBS. Odds to make CFP: +2700 (20th)Odds to win national title: +250000 (T-28th) Week 11 game: 42-32 loss vs. ColoradoWeek 12 game: at West Virginia The Cougars will look back at this season and circle this game as the day the dam broke. Until this matchup, Houston’s losses were to the best teams in the Big 12. But at Folsom Field in Boulder, they learned just what fatigue can lead to: being on the outside looking in at the conference title game and the CFP, yet again. Stat to know: Houston gave up 249 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns to Colorado, both the most it has allowed in a game in three seasons under Willie Fritz. Colorado averaged 6.38 yards per carry. Odds to make CFP: +11000 (29th)Odds to win national title: +200000 (27th) Week 11 game: 48-21 loss vs. GeorgiaWeek 12 game: vs. Kentucky The Tigers got smashed to smithereens. The game was never close — not on the field — which is a shame because a win for Mizzou against this Georgia team would have broken open the SEC and reinserted the Tigers into the College Football Playoff conversation with a chance to host a home game. But now… Stat to know: Missouri allowed a season-high 48 points in the loss to Georgia, its most points surrendered in a game since giving up 49 to LSU on October 7, 2023. Odds to make CFP: N/AOdds to win national title: N/A Week 11 game: 40-39 loss vs. UtahWeek 12 game: at Kansas State The Wildcats played their best football against Utah. But facing the No. 2-ranked team in the country, they fell just a point short. Quarterback Noah Fifita threw for 356 yards with three touchdowns and one pick in yet another game where he furthers his legacy as one of the program’s greatest signal-callers. Stat to know: Quarterback Noah Fifita has thrown for 3,150 yards this season (315.0 per game), ranking third in FBS. His 71.7% completion rate (251-for-350) also ranks third among FBS quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts. Odds to make CFP: +950 (20th)Odds to win national title: +30000 (T-21st) Week 11 game: 22-21 loss vs. TexasWeek 12 game: at Tennessee LSU is paying Lane Kiffin essentially the same amount of money that Kirby Smart and Curt Cignetti did to not make the College Football Playoff. LSU almost certainly won’t contend for a national title this time around, and that makes this season an absolute favor. Stat to know: Saturday marked quarterback Sam Leavitt’s third game this season with multiple turnovers and at least one passing or rushing touchdown, tying him with four other players for the most in the FBS. He also leads the FBS with five red-zone interceptions this season. Odds to make CFP: +100 (12th)Odds to win national title: +1600 (seventh) Week 11 game: 28-7 win vs. BaylorWeek 12 game: at Kansas BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw four interceptions in last week’s loss to Utah. He threw four touchdowns in Saturday's win against the Bears. When he plays well, BYU is capable of beating almost anybody — and certainly a team that fired its head coach in October. Stat to know: Bear Bachmeier is the first BYU quarterback to rush for three touchdowns in a game since Zach Wilson in 2020 against Louisiana Tech. title: Latest On Ketel Marte
content:
Diamondbacks officials met with  Ketel Marte’s agent Charisse Espinosa-Dash during the GM Meetings this week, but the D’Backs “but did not seem to come away with a clear idea about what teams to which Marte would be willing to approve a deal,” the Arizona Republic’s Nick Piecoro writes.  Marte has full no-trade protection as a 10-and-5 player, so even though he is one of the offseason’s most prominent trade candidates, the possibility exists that Marte will remain in Arizona simply because he isn’t interested in changing teams.

It puts the D’Backs in something of an awkward position, especially since the impending lockout will interrupt all transactions activity for what could be months on end.  If Marte isn’t dealt by 10:59pm CT on December 1 (when the current collective bargaining agreement expires and the league is expected to lock out the players), the uncertainty over his future will continue to linger over all of the Diamondbacks’ remaining offseason plans.

As Piecoro puts it, “the Diamondbacks seem to have little choice but to sort of blindly attempt to make the best deal possible without knowing whether Marte will approve it.”  In terms of what that best deal might entail, Piecoro writes that the D’Backs have looked into all variety of trades in their early discussions about Marte — bringing in just prospects, swapping the second baseman for other established big league talents, or a trade package of both veteran and younger talent.

GM Mike Hazen naturally didn’t go into any detail about the Marte negotiations, but the executive expressed some regret at focusing on MLB-ready younger players in past trades of such star players as Zack Greinke or Paul Goldschmidt.  This could hint that Hazen is looking to add just the best talent available (whether that’s current big leaguers or longer-term prospects) while shopping Marte, which is probably a logical approach since Hazen’s options are already limited by Marte’s no-trade leverage.

One option still under consideration is moving Marte for another player on a hefty contract, for salary offset purposes.  The Diamondbacks “did not seem to be leaning in that direction,” as Piecoro says that Arizona’s preference would be to clear some of Marte’s remaining $91.75MM salary off the books and then reinvest that money into other roster needs.  That $91.75MM figure is a little higher than the $87.5MM owed to Marte in the initial terms of his contract, as Piecoro hears from a source that Marte unlocked incentive bonuses based on plate appearances.

The Blue Jays, Giants, Mariners, Phillies, Pirates, Rays, Red Sox, and Tigers all reportedly had some level of interest in Marte last offseason, and Toronto’s interest has continued into this winter.  As MLBTR’s Anthony Franco explored in a recent post about Marte’s potential market, Seattle, San Francisco, and Pittsburgh are probably out of the running based on various factors emerging within the last year.  There’s also the possibility that Marte’s infamous no-show of a game in Boston this past August might have put past suitors or any other teams off entirely.

title: Adalberto Mondesi Attempting Comeback
content:
Former Royals speedster Adalberto Mondesi is trying to get back to the majors, reports Will Sammon, Ken Rosenthal, and Katie Woo of The Athletic. Mondesi is currently playing winter ball in the Dominican Republic. His last big-league stint was in 2022.

Mondesi, 31, has appeared in three games with Aguilas. He’s 4-for-12 with two doubles and a triple so far. He also has four strikeouts. It’s the first live action for Mondesi in four years. He was most recently in Boston’s organization, but knee surgery cost him all of 2023. He was released at the end of the year and never latched on elsewhere.

At his peak, Mondesi was one of the biggest threats on the bases in the league. He stole 75 bases across 2018 and 2019, his first extended look as a big leaguer. He paced the league in triples in 2019. Mondesi led the majors with 24 steals in the shortened 2020 season.

The main drawback in Mondesi’s offensive profile was contact. He punched out at an alarming clip, particularly for a player lacking premier power. Mondesi has a 30.2% strikeout rate over 1,366 career plate appearances.

Mondesi spent time at second base, third base, and shortstop with the Royals. He had up-and-down results as a defender, but generally netted out as a neutral option at each spot. He’s played both second base and shortstop with Aguilas.

Mondesi is still relatively young. He’s a switch-hitter with some defensive versatility. The question would be whether the leg injuries have sapped his best skill. If he isn’t an elite base stealer, it’s hard to see him contributing enough to be worth an MLB roster spot, regardless of his contact issues.

Ryan allegedly kept driving, but the victims caught up to him at a red light. “They said he stepped out of the truck to argue with them, got back in, and drove away,” per the police statement.

Yankees Notes: Bullpen, Morejon, Coaches
content:
The Yankees had the second-best bullpen ERA in the league last season. Maintaining that level will take some work this offseason, with several key pieces hitting free agency.

General manager Brian Cashman referred to the bullpen as New York’s “main priority” during an appearance on MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM this week (h/t Bryan Hoch of MLB.com).

Hoch adds that the Yankees are interested in bringing back two members of the 2026 relief corps, Tim Hill and Paul Blackburn. The team already issued a qualifying offer to closer David Bednar. The former Pirate excelled in his first full season as New York’s stopper and will likely reject the QO. Several teams are known to be in on Hill, including the Mets, Dodgers, Cardinals, Guardians, and Giants.

The club already re-upped with Blackburn once, retaining him on a one-year, $2MM deal last winter. Blackburn originally joined the organization in 2025 after he was cut by the Mets. He struggled in eight games to finish the season and came back on a cheap deal. Blackburn emerged as one of the most effective relievers in the league in 2026, compiling a 1.59 ERA over 85 frames.

[Related: How Paul Blackburn Became An Elite Reliever]

Blackburn ranked 41st on our Top 50 Free Agents list. We predict a two-year, $15MM deal. It’s not a massive price tag, but it’s certainly a step up from Blackburn’s last free agent agreement.

Here are a few other Yankees items…

  • If Bednar rejects the QO, left-hander Adrian Morejon could become a target, per Jorge Castillo of ESPN. The former Padre is the top option in the free agent reliever market. He’s expected to command a hefty contract, both in terms of money and years. Morejon tossed 86 innings with a 2.83 ERA and a 30.4% strikeout rate as the setup man ahead of Mason Miller this past season. There’s been rumblings about teams wanting to stretch him out as a starter, but he prefers to stay in the bullpen.
  • New York is looking for a hitting coach replacement after James Rowson moved on to the Giants. The team has interviewed former Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates for the vacancy, reports Brendan Kuty of The Athletic. Bates has been in L.A. since 2023. He left the Dodgers at the end of the season after failing to reach a contract extension. Hoch notes that Joe Dillon is also a candidate for the hitting coach gig. Dillon has been a hitting coach in the minors and majors for the past decade. He most recently worked for the Cubs’ Double-A affiliate.
  • The Yankees will also have to replace bench coach Brad Ausmus, who was hired as the Astros’ manager. Ausmus is replacing Joe Espada in Houston. The reverse could happen in New York, as Kuty mentions Espada as an option to take over Ausmus’ old role. Espada spent a few seasons as the Yankees’ third base coach in the mid-2010s under former manager Joe Girardi. He moved on to Houston after his time in New York ended, first as a bench coach before replacing Dusty Baker as manager.

title: Kris Bubic Drawing Widespread Interest
content:
While Tarik Skubal is getting the big headlines, another former Dodgers lefty is also drawing plenty of attention. Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic report that Kris Bubic is picking up interest “from contenders and non-contenders alike.”

Bubic has been slowed by arm injuries the past two seasons. His 2025 campaign was cut short by a rotator cuff strain. He made it through nine starts with the Royals to open this past season before going down with elbow soreness. Bubic began a rehab assignment in June, only to be shut down again with renewed elbow issues.

The Dodgers took a flyer on Bubic at the trade deadline, sending over a minor league pitcher in exchange for his services. Bubic made it back as a reliever during the final two weeks of the regular season. He put together five scoreless outings and made the club’s postseason roster. Bubic allowed runs in both of his playoff appearances, taking a loss in the NLDS and a blown save in the NLCS.

The 29-year-old Bubic debuted with Kansas City in 2020. He was a high draft pick and well-regarded prospect in the organization, but spent three seasons as a mediocre starter. Bubic had his 2023 almost entirely wiped out by Tommy John surgery. He returned as a reliever in 2024 and revived his career. The lefty posted a 2.67 ERA with an elite 32.2% strikeout rate in 27 games out of the Royals’ bullpen. Bubic reverted to the rotation in 2025 and delivered 20 starts of a 2.55 ERA and nearly a strikeout per inning.

The double-edged nature of Bubic’s profile brings a variety of suitors into play. A surefire playoff team could see him as a dice roll that could pay off handsomely with minimal investment. A non-playoff team could view him as a cheap route to a premier starter. As our guys put it in the Top 50 Free Agents list, “there aren’t many teams that don’t make sense as a landing spot.”

Bubic just made the cut for those rankings, slotting at No. 48. We predicted a one-year, $12MM deal. Bubic’s health would make a multi-year agreement a bit of a surprise, but a competitive market could encourage a needy team to go that route.

title: Jason Garrett pays heartfelt tribute to Dan Hicks on NBC’s Notre Dame broadcast
content:
The sports media world suffered a devastating loss with the sudden passing of beloved broadcaster Dan Hicks this week at the age of 64. Hicks delivered a remarkable career as a play-by-play broadcaster, headlined by 35 years as a versatile voice for NBC Sports, which included iconic calls in golf and the Olympics.

Additionally, Hicks was NBC’s voice of Notre Dame football from 2014 to 2016 and took over in the prestigious role again in 2024. And in that second stint, Hicks spent the three seasons working alongside Jason Garrett in the NBC booth.

Hicks and Garrett were scheduled to work together again for Saturday’s Notre Dame game against Boston College until the tragic news of Hicks’ death from an acute illness. Jason Benetti stepped in to call the game for NBC and did a beautiful job paying tribute to Hicks throughout the day.

In the moments ahead of kickoff, Benetti delivered an emotional message about being in the booth.

“A campus that was so full of joy this week; our broadcast booth feels very hollow right now here at NBC Sports,” Benetti said. “Our colleague of 35 years, Dan Hicks, passed away on Wednesday. I wish I wasn’t here right now. Jason Benetti, Jason Garrett. I wish Dan was here right now. And I know everybody does.”

“I know how close you and he were, Jason,” Benetti said to Garrett.

Garrett then opened up on the friendship he had with Hicks and explained what a great person Hicks was beyond the broadcasting accolades.

Jason Garrett reflects on his friendship with Dan Hicks, sharing the memories and lasting impact that will stay with him forever. https://t.co/CoKKwPfBmD

— NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 14, 2026

“You know, Hicksy had some of the most iconic calls in any sporting event in history,” Garrett began. “What I always loved about Hicksy, it never was about him. It was always about embracing the moment and highlighting the people involved. And that’s how he lived his life. As legendary a broadcaster as he was, he was a better guy. Devoted husband, and father, and friend. He was always so generous to me in the booth. I can’t tell you the number of times that he would look over to me and say, ‘How you doing? Do you need anything? Can I tee you up?’ That was his line.”

“He had an amazing spirit,” Garrett continued. “He brightened every room that he went into, and he was so funny. We had so much fun together. He told great stories. And he was a great impersonator. He used to do Tom Brokaw, and [Bob Costas], and John Facenda. We actually had him once do JFK. He called a play doing JFK.

“You know, yesterday, you were with us,” Garrett said to Benetti. “Everybody from NBC went over to the Grotto here at Notre Dame to light a candle and say a prayer for him and his family. And I was walking back, and there was a sign on Notre Dame’s campus that said, ‘What does it mean to live a good life?’ And I thought about Hicksy. You know, brightening people’s lives, and striving each day to make the world a better place. And that’s just who he was. That’s why everybody loved him so much. That’s why these tributes that we’ve all seen over the last few days are just remarkable.”

Garrett proceeded to tell his favorite story about Hicks.

“And I have so many stories of him, but my favorite happened right here,” Garrett explained. “Before every game, Notre Dame is a mecca. People come far and wide to see the Irish play football. We had so many people. It’s like Grand Central Station in this booth every week. Whether it’s family, or friends, or former players coming in here, and invariably, it would be like 15 minutes before the game. We’re just about to get going. Hicksy is knee-deep in his preparation.

“And every single time, he would spin his chair around, and he would welcome the people in. It might be two five-year-old kids with their parents and grandparents. And he would show them his spotting board. He’d go over to the telestrator and let them play with that. And show them the view, or the cameras that we had. And we’d get right here in this very spot. And we’d do this team selfie together. And Hicksy didn’t even know these people, but he was right in the middle, hugging them, and smiling with them.

“It’s just who he was. He just went above and beyond trying to make people’s lives better and their day brighter. It’s just who he was and why we loved him so, so much. One of the greatest privileges of my life is to call him my partner and my friend. And we’re going to miss him very, very much.”

“You know how beautiful it is that you’re smiling when you’re thinking about him, though?” Benetti responded.

“He’s the best,” Garrett said.

title: Hoosiers Closing In On Big Ten Title Game? 4 Takeaways From Indiana's Win Over USC
content: Cardiologists in the greater Indianapolis area are slated for a profitable holiday season. Indiana football has never been for the faint of heart. The Hoosiers’ history of ineptitude tested the truest of supporters. But the 2026 season has proved perhaps even more taxing thanks to a heavy dosage of hair pulling-induced play and heart-palpitating finishes. And yet, Indiana is still standing — a 27-13 winner over No. 18 USC. There is nothing particularly complicated about the 2026 Hoosiers. The offense is nowhere near as efficient as last year’s national title-winning squad. The defense? Well, that actually might be better. What that means long-term is that Indiana fans will be either bald or gray whenever this season does reach its ultimate conclusion. But those are conversations for a later date. Curt Cignetti’s bunch continues to find a way. That’s the only thing that matters. Here are my takeaways: 1. The Lincoln Riley Hot Seat Conversation Is Back USC was competitive on Saturday. Give the Trojans that much. There are reasons for hope. Freshman wide receiver Trent Mosley and tight end Mark Bowman look the part of All-Americans now and in the future. Edge rusher Luke Wafle will be the next in a long line of terrorizing Trojans defensive linemen. The combo of Waymond Jordan and King Miller were more effective than any group of rushers has been against this dominant Indiana front-seven. And yet the Trojans still leave Bloomington losers. USC has simply morphed into a mediocre Las Vegas steakhouse. There’s flash. Pizazz. Excitement. But by the time you bite into a premier cut that better rivals your local grocery store and the waiter delivers your $300 bill, everyone is just disappointed and annoyed. Welcome to the Lincoln Riley experience. The Trojans' Week 9 win over Ohio State was supposed to be cathartic — so much so that Riley decided to scrawl a slew of thoughts onto a piece of paper he’d kept tucked in his back pocket for the postgame press conference, which made for a weird scene. It only further proved USC’s head coach continues to feel the walls closing in. The Buckeyes — even in a win on Saturday over Northwestern — have shown they are far from the team that came to Indiana and beat the Hoosiers thanks to six inches of sideline a month ago. Beyond that, USC’s best win this fall is …. Penn State? Washington? You get the point. Riley was hired with hopes of College Football Playoff glory. The Trojans haven’t so much as sniffed the field since Caleb Williams was on campus. A win over a beatable Indiana team on Saturday would’ve thrust the Trojans back into the conversation. Too many mistakes. Too many misfires. Too many unfinished opportunities. The loss now means the most hyped battle for Los Angeles in decades is the only thing separating USC from potentially its third eight-win or worse season in four years. That won’t cut it for the check writers. That won’t cut it for the stakeholders in Heritage Hall. Assuming USC can hold serve against a head coach-less Maryland team next week, Riley may have only one more shot to prove he deserves to remain in charge in Los Angeles. That game result may deserve its own set of prepared statements. 2. Indiana Finished Drives When It Mattered. USC Didn’t. USC looked the part early. The Trojans rushed for almost 5 yards per carry over the course of their first six rushes, while quarterback Jayden Maiava made a handful of feathery completions as they marched down to the Indiana 14-yard line. And then it all fell apart. A hold pulled USC out of the red zone. Miller was stonewalled on a 1-yard rush. Maiava’s third down throw to Mosley was broken up. It all concluded with kicker Ryon Sayeri ringing a 51-yard field goal attempt off the left upright into the shaded South End Zone at Memorial Stadium. Perfect. No notes. The Trojans followed up their first drive with an almost identical effort on their second possession. They marched 63 yards on 12 plays thanks to a steady mix of passing and rushing as Indiana’s normally stifling defense struggled to match Maiava on a handful of run-pass options. A third-down roughing the passer penalty and an 8-yard pass from Maiava to Jordan pushed the Trojans inside the Indiana 15-yard line. Then, Jordan was promptly stuffed for a 1-yard rush, lost four on his next carry and Maiava misfired on a third-down throw to the front left pylon that bounced off Bowman’s outstretched hands. The Trojans settled for a field goal. Compare that to the Hoosiers. Indiana responded to USC’s opening drive by marching 60 yards on six plays — the entirety of which came on a pair of big-time throws from quarterback Grant Wilson, who started on Saturday in place of the injured Josh Hoover. Wilson wasn’t perfect. He underthrew wide receiver Nick Marsh down the sideline on the Hoosiers’ first play from scrimmage. He was almost intercepted on a toss to the back right pylon on a throw that floated on him longer than he intended. Still, Indiana managed to finish drives when it mattered. USC didn’t. If that’s not an encapsulation of both programs at the moment, I’m not sure what is. 3. New Quarterback, Same Problems For Indiana Saturday started with a bang. The deep throw to Marsh. The touchdown toss to tight end Brock Schott. Indiana’s offense was rolling. Until it wasn’t. Wilson had moments in Saturday’s contest. He flashed an ability to push the ball vertically to the loaded Hoosier receiver room in a way that Hoover hadn’t in recent weeks — a game-clinching 42-yard toss to wide receiver Charlie Becker proving to be the highlight of the day. But the inconsistencies were there against a USC secondary that ranked in the bottom half of FBS and 13th in the Big Ten in passing defense heading into Saturday’s affair in Bloomington. Pushing for points before the end of the second quarter, Wilson missed an open Shazz Preston on a ball that was high and outside, before bounding into the arms of USC defensive back Deven Bryant. The Trojans took that gift and marched 60 yards in three plays, capping off the half-ending drive with a 7-yard touchdown connection between Maiava and wide receiver Zacharyus Williams to knot the proceedings at 10 points apiece. Sound familiar? It should. Hoover, to his credit, has also flashed this fall. But far too often he was off target, off kilter and out of sync. How much of that is injury-induced is hard to say. We likely won’t know for sure until season’s end. Yet for all the decries that Indiana needed to make a quarterback change in recent weeks, Saturday further cemented, if nothing else, that the Hoosiers seem destined to go as far as their defense will carry them. Is Cignetti’s bunch really just Michigan with better receivers and more late-game bravado? It’s getting harder to beat the allegations. 4. Indiana, UCLA On A Collision Course For The Big Ten Title Game The final Big Ten title game is on pace to include *checks notes* Indiana and UCLA. Just like we all expected. The Hoosiers are in the driver's seat with a one-game edge over Ohio State with just Washington and Purdue remaining on its schedule. The trip to Seattle, while long, looks far less imposing given the Huskies' similar inability to put together anything offensively this fall. Bob Chesney's bunch, meanwhile, kicked back at home and watched the rest of the Big Ten beat itself up after the Bruins notched a rain-soaked win over a pesky Illinois team on Friday night. UCLA is 10-0 for the first time since 1998. Its remaining schedule includes a Michigan team that has set back offensive football eight decades and a USC squad that, while talented, continues to struggle to put away the conference's best. The storylines for this hypothetical matchup are juicy. Cignetti against the man who replaced him at James Madison. Indiana against the program plenty have pegged as the 2026 version of the Hoosiers. A sportswriter can dream, eh? Two games remain. We might be able to start mapping out those Indianapolis story plans.

title: Astros AGM Connor Huff Resigns
content:
The Astros have made a pair of major staffing additions this offseason, hiring Randy Flores as general manager and Brad Ausmus as skipper. The club also had a subtraction this week, with Flores announcing that assistant general manager Connor Huff has left the organization.

Flores told reporters, including Chandler Rome of The Athletic, that Huff resigned to take a “new, exciting opportunity outside of baseball.” Huff had been with the team since 2022. He was promoted from vice president of business and baseball operations to AGM at the end of the 2025 season. Huff replaced former assistant GM Andrew Ball.

Houston still has two AGMs on staff, Gavin Dickey and Charles Cook. Both interviewed for the role that ultimately went to Flores. Houston had a vacancy in its top front office position after moving on from Dana Brown in August. Flores mentioned that he’d been given the go-ahead to hire a replacement for Huff, though he didn’t specify whether it would be for an AGM role or a different position.

The Astros are looking to rebound after an uneven year. Brown was fired with a month left in the regular season. Manager Joe Espada was retained at the time, but it was pretty clear he wouldn’t be with the club beyond 2026. Houston backed into a division title despite a .500 record and was quickly booted from the playoffs in a sweep by the White Sox.

title: NBC’s Tim Howard: Pep Guardiola ‘absolutely not the right manager’ for USMNT
content:
Most American soccer fans will likely be thrilled to see reports this week linking legendary Spanish coach Pep Guardiola’s name linked to the USMNT.

But NBC’s Tim Howard, who not only covered Guardiola’s Manchester City squads for the past decade on television but also starred for the USMNT during his playing career, is tempering that excitement.

While reacting to the rumors on his podcast Unfiltered Soccer this week, Howard said Guardiola is “absolutely not the right manager” for the USMNT based on how long of a commitment the Americans need ahead of the next World Cup, as well as Guardiola’s challenging temperament with players.

“Pep Guardiola has only ever succeeded with tier-one players,” Howard said. “People might get upset with this, we have probably tier-three players, globally.”

“But Pep Guardiola, [at FC] Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Manchester City … has succeeded, OK? We actually, me, you and every other football fan in the world, we actually don’t know if Pep Guardiola is a good manager coaching level-two or -three players. We do not know.”

Howard explained that part of the reason Guardiola may only be effective coaching top-flight talent is that he is incredibly demanding of players.

“Pep Guardiola has crushed players,” Howard said. “Crushed players that would walk into our national team, and they’d be the best player by, like, three thousand miles. And those players, because of how hard Pep is, withered. So he’s not the guy for me.”

Mauricio Pochettino, who was fielding interest from top clubs in Europe starting before the North American World Cup last summer, is leaving the USMNT for Manchester United. Leaders at U.S. Soccer are expected to talk with Guardiola this upcoming week.

The USMNT will compete in the Concacaf Gold Cup in 2027, followed by the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. Hopes remain high that the USMNT’s “golden generation,” led by Christian Pulisic, can deliver on their promise in what could be their final World Cup, in 2030.

The recent influx of cash to U.S. Soccer means it is finally possible for the USMNT to pursue the likes of Pochettino or Guardiola, but Howard is taking a more realistic approach and arguing that Guardiola is not the right fit.

USA Routs Haiti A Day After Pochettino-to-Man United Becomes Official: 5 Takeaways
content: NU STADIUM (Miami) — In its first competitive match since the 2026 World Cup — and its penultimate game with Mauricio Pochettino as the coach before the Argentine takes over Manchester United — the U.S. men’s national team trounced Haiti on Saturday in the opening leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal. Center back Auston Trusty opened the USA’s account in the first half when he redirected a Sebastian Berhalter free kick past Les Grenadiers keeper Alexandre Pierre, Christian Pulisic scored twice and 18-year-old striker Julian Hall converted his fourth goal in five games since making his debut in September. Midfielder Weston McKennie added the fifth before striker Folarin Balogun came off the bench to complete the scoring with about eight minutes of regular time remaining. Saturday’s contest was played in front of a heavily pro-Haitian crowd in South Florida; the Caribbean country was given permission by Concacaf to host its "home" leg at Inter Miami’s recently opened 27,000-seat venue because of security issues in Port-au-Prince, the nation's capital. The Miami area boasts the largest Haitian ex-patriot population in the U.S. The teams meet again on Tuesday in Cincinnati in the back half of the aggregate-goals-wins series, with the Stars and Stripes now all but certain to advance to March’s final four in Los Angeles. Here are my takeaways from Saturday’s contest. The USA kicked off preparations for the opener under a cloud of speculation. Before all 25 of the players Pochettino summoned had even reported to U.S. Soccer’s training center in greater Atlanta, there were reports that the former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton boss could be bound for Old Trafford. Veteran defender Antonee "Jedi" Robinson admitted that he and his teammates were aware of the news, but that it would be business as usual until the 54-year-old’s departure was confirmed. Other players said the same in the days that followed, though by Thursday the sense of inevitability had become obvious. Pochettino told his players that morning. On Friday, both U.S. Soccer and Manchester United made it official. The American players handled the situation professionally during the week, but Saturday was always going to tell the real story. And to their credit, there was no sign that the roller-coaster of emotions they’d experienced in the days prior had any impact on how they performed. Not negatively, anyway. Against a notoriously physical and stingy Haiti team, which played in the World Cup for the first time in more than five decades earlier this year, the U.S. was sharp and committed. It’s clear they want to send Poch off on a high note. After 90 dominant minutes, they’re halfway there. "They were very, very professional from Day 1 when they started to see all the rumors," Pochettino told me in his post-match press conference.  "We feel so proud about the players and how they managed this type of situation." No player took more heat for the Americans’ lopsided, World Cup-ending 4-1 loss to Belgium in the round of 16 than the program’s longtime headliner. The criticism of Pulisic, who went scoreless in four games, didn’t subside even after it was revealed that he’d suffered a double microfracture in his right leg. But the 28-year-old has been rounding into form with AC Milan in recent weeks, and in his first appearance for his country since the World Cup, he earned Man of the Match honors on the strength of his brace — the first time he’s scored twice in one game a U.S. jersey since June 2023. "It was great to see everyone, great performance from the team, good to be back in the mix and scoring some goals and winning the game," Pulisic said. "I'm happy. Hopefully, I can score a few more." Heading into the final FIFA window of 2026, the 28-year-old had been enjoying a career year. With just five caps to his credit beforehand, the left-footed center-back parlayed a strong March camp into a World Cup roster spot, then scored against Türkiye in the tournament co-hosts’ final group stage match. He and Chris Richards anchored the USA’s back line last month in a 3-0 victory over Mexico in front of a huge pro-El Tri crowd in Arizona. But Trusty and his family suffered a tragedy a few weeks later, when his father, Walt, died. The Philadelphia area native took a leave from Celtic, his Scottish club, and hadn’t played at all in almost a whole month, since Celtic’s 4-1 Europa League loss to Benfica on Oct. 15. He scored less than 10 minutes into his return. "To score that goal and also to have the win today, it really meant a lot," he said. "The past few weeks have been very, very tough. Probably the toughest of my life. "I'm very, very proud to score today." The USA’s second goal was a beautiful team effort. It started more than 100 yards away from Pierre’s net, with six passes between Alex Freeman, McKennie, Berhalter, Pulisic, and Robinson before Hall finished the sequence with aplomb. U.S. fans had reason to celebrate beyond Hall’s latest goal. Because this was an official game, and because Hall had already made more than three appearances for the Americans, he’s permanently cap-tied to the country for the rest of his international career. The New York City product had previously been eligible for Poland through his mother. Three subs – Mathis Albert, Justin Ellis, Adri Mehmeti – also became cap-tied when they came off the bench. "It's an honor to play for this country," Hall told me. "I'm just looking forward to keep making an impact." Saturday’s victory was the fifth in a row for the U.S. after the exhibition wins over El Tri, Canada, Chile and Peru earlier this fall. In what is expected to be a pro-USA crowd in southern Ohio next week, Pochettino’s team will try to send him off with a perfect 6-0 record before he takes over Man United next Wednesday. "We just have to try to continue to grow as a team," Pulisic said. "He brought a lot of excitement to the team, so I think he'll leave that behind."

content:
Jordan Davis had barely unpacked in Jacksonville before he introduced the local press corps to his house rules.

The Jaguars acquired the 26-year-old defensive tackle from the Eagles on Nov. 9, sending Philadelphia a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick a day before the trade deadline. Davis was the third defender Jacksonville landed that Monday, after safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux, as the 6-2 Jaguars pushed their chips toward a Super Bowl run.

When Davis met Jacksonville reporters for the first time, though, the opening order of business had nothing to do with run fits or his new defensive coordinator. Instead, he wanted the room to understand how he settles a collision of voices.

“I have a policy when it comes to the media. When a lady is talking, and it’s like two questions at once, the lady always gets the right of way,” he said. “So I just want y’all to know that.”

title: Pirates Want To Limit Ryan O’Hearn’s Outfield Reps
content:
The Pirates have Oneil Cruz and Bryan Reynolds as everyday options in center and left field, respectively. Right field is more of a question mark, as general manager Ben Cherington outlined this week at the GM Meetings.

Cherington told reporters, including Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, that the club is looking to construct a team that doesn’t require Ryan O’Hearn to spend much time on the grass. The plan would be to have him rotate at first base and DH with Spencer Horwitz. Cherington added that ideally, O’Hearn makes just the occasional start or late-game appearance in right field.

Pittsburgh signed O’Hearn to a two-year, $29MM deal last winter. He was expected to split his time between right field and first base, with fellow free agent acquisition Marcell Ozuna handling the majority of the DH work. That’s largely how it played out, with O’Hearn making 42 starts in right field and 36 at first base. Ozuna’s ill-fated tenure with the team ended in August. O’Hearn ended up making 25 starts at DH.

[Related: Ryan O’Hearn’s Adjustments In Pittsburgh]

Capping O’Hearn’s opportunities in the outfield makes sense on multiple fronts. He posted -5 Defensive Runs Saved at the position in 2026. For his career, he’s at -16 DRS. O’Hearn has typically graded out poorly at first base as well, though he’s had some decent years over there. Perhaps more notably, O’Hearn had two separate stints on the IL with quad strains last year. The second instance cost him nearly six weeks in the second half and hurt Pittsburgh’s offense during the stretch run.

With O’Hearn sticking to first base and DH, more opportunities would seem to be available for Esmerlyn Valdez. The Magician hit 17 homers in just 72 games as a rookie. A hamstring injury cut his season short but isn’t expected to impact his 2027 campaign.

Cherington didn’t exactly hand Valdez the job, though. The exec said Valdez has “some earning to do” before taking over as the everyday guy in right. The rookie’s power production came with a massive 37.6% strikeout rate. Valdez also cooled off significantly after a red-hot first month. He posted a .662 OPS in August. He was hitting .125 in September before going down with the hamstring strain.

Like O’Hearn, Valdez was not an asset with the glove last season. He posted -6 DRS in 72 appearances between the corner outfield spots. The majority of his starts came in right field.

The internal option to pick up playing time in right field would be Jake Mangum. He had a decent first year in Pittsburgh after coming over in the trade from the Rays. Mangum was a positive defender and stole 23 bases as a semi-regular option at all three spots. He’s a fairly typical fourth outfielder type, but can be useful in a part-time role.

Beazley notes that Pittsburgh won’t rule out adding in the corners. A righty-swinging outfielder would seem like a logical choice with Valdez and O’Hearn both being left-handed. Well-traveled veterans Randal Grichuk, Ramon Laureano, and Austin Hays fit the mold, though they might be on the hunt for consistent playing time. Old friend Tommy Pham also belongs in the group. The Pirates might be better off banking on Valdez taking the job, knowing they can fall back on O’Hearn and Mangum if needed.

title: Jason Benetti had a sweet tribute for Dan Hicks after Notre Dame touchdown
content:
Beloved broadcaster Dan Hicks died unexpectedly this week at the age of 64.

Since then, tributes for Hicks have poured in from across the sporting world, including some from his fellow broadcasters, and others from the athletes whose biggest moments were shared with the masses with the help of his singular voice.

Hicks was known widely as NBC’s voice of golf, as well his role calling several prominent Olympic sports, and as the voice of Notre Dame football for the network. Given the suddenness of his passing, NBC turned to fellow commentator Jason Benetti to step in on short notice to call Saturday’s game for the Irish against Boston College.

It was clear that Benetti did not take his job lightly, and he paid tribute to Hicks several times throughout the day. While opening the broadcast, Benetti encouraged viewers to check in on those they are close with.

“A classic college football rivalry, in classic college football weather,” Benetti said just before kickoff. “The Fighting Irish and the Eagles. And today is one of those days where you remember, for us at NBC Sports, how communal college football is, and how much we enjoy watching this game with the people we care about. Today’s one of those days where, if you’re so inclined, tell the people around you — or the people on your text thread — you appreciate them, and you care about them.”

title: Tim Brando bashes Greg Sankey over broadcaster criticism
content:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey has had a lot to say over the past week.

Appearing as a guest with Paul Finebaum, Sankey offered critiques of the rival Big Ten, arguing against those that implied that an underlying pro-SEC bias helped the conference.

But Sankey’s harshest words came for some of those in the broadcast booth. The commissioner took issue with several commentators who criticized the officiating in a few big SEC games the previous weekend.

“I am highly disappointed in announcers and their criticism, and they’re wrong,” Sankey told Finebaum. “Some of the worst officials in America are those in the announce booth. We have officiating experts who I turned on a game on Saturday, who was just flat wrong. And what that creates is this narrative that we’ve done something wrong, and that is unacceptable to me, and we have to address that.”

While Sankey didn’t directly name names while speaking with Finebaum, it was later reported that his comments were largely aimed at former Georgia quarterback and current SEC Network analyst Aaron Murray, who was critical of the officiating in the Missouri-Texas game, as well as ESPN play-by-play man Sean McDonough, who raised questions about the crew calling the Georgia-Ole Miss game.

On Friday, McDonough’s fellow broadcaster Tim Brando took some time out of his interview with Jacksonville sports radio station 1010XL to lay into Sankey for offering input in places where he wasn’t welcome. The conversation began with a discussion around some of the officiating that was questioned in the first place, before Brando directed some of his ire at the SEC commissioner, noting that the broadcasters were only voicing what many people were thinking.

“What the hell is Greg Sankey throwing ESPN and ABC announcers under the bus for?” Brando asked. “I’ve talked to Sean [McDonough]. He knows about it. And he had [Missouri head coach Eli] Drinkwitz in that game, and Eli obviously had tons of problems with what happened in the Texas game, and Eli told Sean exactly what the issue was.”

Brando theorized that Sankey’s frustrations may be stemming from other issues, and didn’t buy his excuses for the conference not being as transparent with its reviews as others have become this year.

“I’m just going to tell you right now pal, this guy is out of control,” he said of Sankey. “I don’t know if it’s because [Big Ten commissioner Tony] Petitti got his way and he got 24 teams. Plus the fact that Sankey really didn’t want to go to 24, and everyone knows he didn’t [want to go to 24].

“I don’t know what’s bothering Greg, but to say that ‘Oh we want to do it right when we go to the command center.’ Here’s the issue. He knows that the ACC has a command center, Big Ten has a command center, Big 12 has a command center. Now there are times when I’m listening to the command centers when I’m calling a game, and I can get confused because I hear several people talking. But you know what? To the viewer, and even to the broadcaster, I’ve got a better understanding to what they’re thinking before the call is made. So that’s good. That’s transparency.”

Brando offered that there were plenty of voices more qualified to offer their opinions on a game’s officiating, and essentially told Sankey to stay in his lane.

“And if it’s Pereira or Blandino that come in afterwards, or, he’s got his own guy, his own SEC guy, his own past supervisor on ABC helping with this, and he’s still got a problem with the announcers? Greg, why don’t you just do your job and make sure the fans and the viewers and the networks you’re in business with all get the same access? For some reason the SEC says they’re above all that and they want it to be a clean, crisp broadcast. They don’t want any confusion. Who anointed him the king of broadcasting? Has he won any Emmys? I don’t think so.”

That Sankey is going to defend his conference against its critics is no surprise, but Brando’s retort puts his critiques in a good perspective. Everyone watching a game, from the broadcast team to the halftime announcers to the fans at home and in the stadium has the right to call it like they see it when it comes to how things are being officiated.

Football is filled with objective and subjective calls, and sometimes they’re going to go your way, and other times they won’t. That’s just how it works. Getting frustrated with the people who point that out is like getting frustrated with football itself.

The LG Twins of the KBO announced a contract extension for first baseman Austin Dean this week. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $2MM.

He has 11 more long balls than the next-closest player in that span, which happens to be Si Hwan Roh, who was recently posted for MLB teams by the Hanwha Eagles.

The 33-year-old Dean was drafted by the Marlins in the fourth round of the 2012 draft. He hit well in the minors, but didn’t debut with Miami until 2018. Dean posted a .656 OPS in parts of two seasons as a Marlin. He was dealt to the Cardinals in a minor trade before the 2020 campaign.

After playing sparingly in the shortened season, Dean broke camp with the Cardinals in 2021. He saw minimal work off the bench and was sent down a month into the year. Dean was bumped off the roster at the end of the season and claimed by the Giants. He spent the majority of his time in San Francisco’s organization at Triple-A.

Dean was a subpar outfielder in the majors, recording -15 Defensive Runs Saved in 96 games. He’s played almost exclusively first base and DH with the Twins. The power-hitting righty with limited defensive viability tends to be a tough roster fit in the majors. It might be difficult for Dean to find a gig if he tried to make a return to the majors. Pat McAfee showed up to ‘College GameDay’ on a horse
content:
ESPN’s traveling road show College GameDay was in Boise, Idaho on Saturday for the first time in 16 years ahead of No. 24 Boise State’s showdown with Oregon State. With a win, the Broncos can secure their spot in the Pac-12 title game and continue their march towards a potential spot in the College Football Playoff.

It was a packed house for GameDay, with Boise State fans showing up in droves despite the early call-time — it was still dark out when the show first went on the air. Notably, Pat McAfee was absent from the GameDay desk at the very start of the show, but only because he was waiting to make a grand entrance.

“As you might have heard, people have had some travel difficulties,” host Rece Davis teased, referencing the nationwide flight delays that made travel impossible for much of Friday. “That includes Pat McAfee. Pat is trying to find his way here. We’re certainly hopeful that we find him soon, and that McAfee can make it to the set.”

At that point, McAfee called out, “Rece! Rece Davis can you hear me?” Cameras cut to McAfee riding on horseback alongside Boise State handlers and representatives carrying a school flag.

“Don’t you worry about an airplane. Don’t you worry about an automobile. I’m riding on Rodeo. A horse, that was of course, built to be amongst these Broncos fans,” McAfee said, throwing in some “Whoaaaaaaas” when necessary as his horse got a little excited.

“Thank you Kathy Joe, you’re the best,” McAfee said as he dismounted. He then thanked the rest of the crew that helped him in and began running towards the desk.

“This particular Saturday is going to be a magical one,” McAfee said. “There’s going to be chaos, implications across the country as people will be punching their ticket to the College Football Playoff.”

Once at the desk, McAfee exhaled a bit.

“That horse’s name was Rodeo, and I will say to Rodeo, thank you for not bucking my ass off. A magical morning here at Boise State. I’ve never ridden a horse before. I certainly lied to them to let that happen.”

Rece Davis: “And as you might have heard, people have had some travel difficulties… That includes Pat McAfee…”

title: A’s Receiving Trade Interest In Jacob Wilson
content:
Jacob Wilson’s All-Star rookie season was followed up by an injury-plagued 2026 campaign, as the Athletics’ shortstop hit only .266/.298/.388 over 337 plate appearances.  Wilson sprained his left shoulder in May while diving for a Gunnar Henderson grounder, and while he missed only a month on the injured list, renewed shoulder discomfort sent him back to the IL for good in late August, and Wilson underwent a season-ending surgery on his troublesome shoulder in early September.

Despite this rough sophomore year and the $66MM remaining on Wilson’s contract, the shortstop has been drawing trade interest, according to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale.  This could just be some due diligence from rival clubs, or explorations to see if the A’s would bite on a lowball offer.  There isn’t any indication that the A’s are even considering moving Wilson, and a trade would be pretty surprising given that Wilson signed his long-term extension with the club just last January.

It should be noted that Wilson’s extension was signed under former GM David Forst, so new president of baseball operations Taylor Smith could have a different view of Wilson as a long-term cornerstone.  There haven’t been any updates on Wilson’s recovery timeline, so if he will miss a decent chunk of the 2027 season, that also might impact the Athletics’ willingness to consider trade possibilities.  That said, one would also imagine clubs wouldn’t be willing to trade for Wilson without a long look at his medicals in the wake of his surgery.

The sixth overall pick of the 2023 draft, Wilson made his big league debut barely over a year after his draft date, and played in 28 games for the A’s during the 2024 campaign.  He then broke out by hitting .311/.355/.444 with 13 homers over 523 PA in 2025, finishing second in AL Rookie of the Year voting and also earning some down-ballot MVP votes.  Luis Arraez is the most frequent comp for Wilson’s game, as Wilson rarely strikes out and makes a ton of contact, even if he doesn’t often make hard contact.

Defensively, Wilson’s glovework drew below-average grades in 2025, and the Defensive Runs Saved gave him a -6 mark in 2026.  The Outs Above Average metric was much more favorable, as Wilson went from -3 OAA in 2025 (over 1053 2/3 innings at shortstop) to +9 (over 637 1/3 innings) in 2026.  These defensive questions could be a moot point if top shortstop prospect Leo De Vries lives up to expectations and Wilson is shifted over to second or third base, though De Vries’ timeline has been delayed by a shoulder surgery of his own, and is expected to be out until at least May 2027.

Moving Wilson would create another hole in the A’s infield and less of a safety net for De Vries’ eventual arrival in the majors.  That said, Smith could acquire a veteran shortstop as a stopgap, or use an internal option like Joshua Kuroda-Grauer or Alika Williams.  Offering Wilson could potentially help the Athletics land a much-needed dose of young pitching help, and maybe also a veteran pitcher on a larger salary to offset part of Wilson’s $66MM price tag.  It isn’t exactly a “bad contract swap” situation given Wilson’s youth and future potential, though his salary does create another obstacle in any trade talks the A’s could explore.

While a Wilson trade seems unlikely, Smith may have to resort to creative tactics in order to upgrade the Athletics’ pitching in both the short and long term.  Free agents obviously aren’t exactly rushing to spend time in Sacramento’s hitter-friendly ballpark, and it remains to be seen if the Athletics’ new home in Las Vegas might also favor batters.

title: Robert Griffin III counters Desmond Howard over Jeremiah Smith’s Heisman case: ‘Stop hating’
content:
Two of the most prominent Heisman Trophy winners in college football media are going at it over the favorite for this year’s award, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

Earlier this week in an appearance on ESPN’s First Take, Desmond Howard questioned Smith’s ability to make a “difference” in “the biggest games.” Howard argued that the case against Smith winning the Heisman went deeper than Ohio State losing its starting quarterback to injury, and that Smith did not have enough superstar “moments” to deserve the award.

Many raised an eyebrow at Howard’s impassioned argument against Smith — widely seen as the best player in college football this year — because Howard is an alum of Ohio State’s rival, Michigan.

The comments clearly drew a reaction across the media as well. During Fox’s broadcast of Ohio State-Northwestern on Saturday, game analyst and former Baylor star Robert Griffin III addressed Howard directly, calling on the College GameDay panelist to “stop hating” and uphold his place in the “Heisman brotherhood.”

“When you talk about the Heisman Trophy, my guy Desmond Howard, he’s been very critical of Jeremiah Smith and said, ‘When does this guy ever show up in big-time games?'” Griffin said on the call. “Well, he’s shown up in big-time games all over the place, and Desmond Howard has to stop hating on Jeremiah Smith just because he goes to Ohio State. That’s not the right way to do this, and we’ve got to be better in our Heisman brotherhood.”

https://t.co/PIzpzIJyiT

— welovesports40 (@welovesports40) November 14, 2026

Separate from his bias as a Michigan man, Howard’s criticism of Smith doesn’t really hold up. Smith caught eight passes for 144 yards in last year’s No. 1 vs. No. 2 bout in the Big Ten championship game, and then went for 157 yards and a touchdown in the College Football Playoff quarters. This season, Smith caught eight balls for 164 yards and a score early on against Texas, and broke the 200-yard mark with two touchdowns against Iowa three weeks later. Even as the Buckeyes dropped back-to-back games to USC and Oregon, Smith broke 80 yards and scored in each game.

While Griffin certainly relishes conflict with other media figures, it’s not hard to see why he called Howard out in this case. Howard took a cheap shot at a gifted and promising young star, making poor use of his immense platform on ESPN. And as a top analyst at Fox, which airs just about every Ohio State game, it is no surprise that Griffin would defend the program and its best player.

Obviously there’s plenty of familiarity between the two sides, and Iglesias has continue to pitch so well that there isn’t much concern of a slowdown even after he enters his age-37 season.  The Athletic’s Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal note that re-signing Iglesias to strengthen the bullpen would increase the chance that the Braves will use Didier Fuentes as a starter next season, though Atlanta figures to add a more proven starter even if Fuentes is indeed stretched out in Spring Training.

More from around the NL East…

  • The Nationals had one of baseball’s worst bullpens in 2026, but while improving the relief corps is an obvious offseason goal, “relievers who command multiple years and significant money are probably off the table,” the Athletic’s Spencer Nusbaum writes.  Since even contending teams often take this stance in acquiring relief help, it isn’t too surprising that the still-rebuilding Nats aren’t being too aggressive in adding the bullpen problem, even if Washington did exceed expectations with 77 wins last year.  The rotation also needs help, and to this end D.C. seems more aggressive, as Nusbaum said the Nats have “asked around about controllable starting pitching in trade talks, and is casting a wider net than last season.”
  • In other Nationals news, Nusbaum reports that the team has hired John Morris as the team’s new VP of baseball research.  The role puts Morris in charge of “the baseball side of the Nats analytics department,” as per Nusbaum.  Morris comes to Washington from New York, where he worked as the Yankees’ assistant director of quantitative analysis.
  • The Marlins have hired Trayce Thompson for a role in their baseball operations department, the Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson reports.  The news presumably means the 35-year-old Thompson is retiring after a pro career that saw him play in parts of seven MLB seasons from 2015-23, and Thompson has spent the last three years in the minors, the Mexican League, in independent baseball, and playing for Great Britain’s World Baseball Classic team.  Thompson played for five different clubs at the MLB level, with 217 of his 369 career games coming in a Dodgers uniform.  The ex-outfielder’s best sustained offensive performance was a second-half surge with the 2022 Dodgers, and Thompson will finish his career with 45 homers and a .212/.300/.411 slash line in 1058 plate appearances in the bigs.  MLB Trade Rumors congratulates Thompson on a fine career, and we wish him with the best as he begins this new direction in his baseball life.

Paul Finebaum eviscerates Oklahoma AD, defends SEC over Ole Miss postponement
content:
The game between the Oklahoma Sooners and Ole Miss Rebels is the only major college football contest shifted to Sunday in the wake of the FAA ground stop affecting flights across the nation.

While several games had to adjust start times, Ole Miss was seemingly the only one that couldn’t make it to their destination in time to play the game on Saturday. The situation drew a strong rebuke from Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny. He issued a blistering statement about the postponement, even saying that the SEC threatened the school with a forfeit if they didn’t agree to the rescheduling.

It’s clear Oklahoma is unhappy because of the logistics of the move and the impact it will have on its fans planning to attend or watch the game. And maybe it is peculiar that Ole Miss is the only school unable to travel to keep the game on Saturday and didn’t want to take a long bus ride to make it happen on schedule.

But on SEC Nation, Paul Finebaum had no sympathy for the Sooners. In fact, he stuck up for the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey and had strong words for Denny for not thinking of the conference as a whole and everyone else who had to navigate unprecedented circumstances.

Paul Finebaum: “I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss… What I don’t think is correct is [Oklahoma AD Roger Denny] pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever…” https://t.co/k124Yv7Ocq

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 14, 2026

“I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss. But I believe the administration and Ole Miss did everything they could. What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know,” Finebaum said.

“Mr. Denny, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone. He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fanbase. And what Roger Denny has been doing all this year is pandering to his fanbase.”

Finebaum then cited Denny giving head coach Brent Venables a contract extension and underperforming this season, far away from College Football Playoff contention. He then called Denny an “impulsive leader” and even noted his former career as a tax attorney. In saying Oklahoma runs differently than other programs in the conference, he then added that it was “against the code of the SEC.”

“What he did here is really against the code of the SEC to call out a commissioner during a national crisis and emergency. He’s thinking about himself and his fanbase, who’s already on tenderhooks because of the season, and I think he is dead wrong and quite frankly, I think it’s unbecoming of a leader in college athletics or anywhere to do what he did,” Finebaum added.

It’s interesting that Paul Finebaum would reference the “code” of the SEC in the same week that commissioner Greg Sankey called out ESPN announcers for not showing enough deference to the league’s officials. We’ll see if the whole saga provides Oklahoma with some added motivation for the game on Sunday if they feel like the entire SEC machine has turned against them.
