title: Dodgers Interested In Jonathan Loaisiga, Tim Hill
content:
Right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga and left-hander Tim Hill are two of the relievers on the Dodgers’ radar, according to (respectively) ESPN’s Jesse Rogers and the New York Post’s Jon Heyman.  Rogers notes that Loaisiga is “getting closer” to landing a deal, so a signing might come sooner rather than later.

Beyond Los Angeles, Loaisiga and Hill have also each drawn interest from the Yankees (their mutual former team) and Mets.  The Blue Jays have been linked to Loaisiga as well, and Rogers suggests that at least one other team is also in on the right-hander.  The Guardians, Giants, and Cardinals have all been linked to Hill in previous reports.

For Loaisiga in particular, this healthy market is a terrific outcome for a pitcher who had to settle for a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks last winter.  The righty had shown flashes of being an elite relief arm during his eight seasons with the Yankees, yet injuries continually kept Loaisiga on the sidelines.  New York declined a $5MM club option on Loaisiga after the 2025 season, and he was both healthy and very effective in delivering a 2.42 ERA over 67 innings out of Arizona’s pen in 2026.

While Loaisiga doesn’t rack up many strikeouts, he induces a ton of grounders and a lot of soft contact, plus he has a strong 6.3% walk rate in 260 innings since the start of the 2020 season.  MLB Trade Rumors ranked Loaisiga 45th on our top 50 free agents list and projected a two-year, $13MM contract, making him a potential bargain for a lot of teams provided the 32-year-old can again avoid the injury bug.

Now entering his age-37 season, Hill has a similar resume as a grounder-heavy control pitcher who rarely records strikeouts.  Hill has continued to dominate left-handed batters but righties hit him pretty well, and a big spike in his home run totals led to Hill’s 4.60 ERA over 58 2/3 innings for the Yankees last season.  Hill is the type of reliever who would’ve held more appeal prior to the introduction of the three-batter rule, but the veteran is still a logical target for clubs in need of left-handed bullpen help.

The Dodgers have hopes of re-signing Alex Vesia, and Tanner Scott, Justin Wrobleski, and Jack Dreyer are among the left-handed bullpen options remaining on the L.A. roster.  Still, Hill would further bolster this group, and it’s not hard to imagine the Dodgers adding both Hill and Loaisiga as part of their goal of amassing pitching for another extended playoff run.  The right-handed side of the Los Angeles pen took a hit when Evan Phillips signed with the Braves, perhaps increasing the Dodgers’ interest in Loaisiga.

title: TKO CEO Ari Emanuel blames Pete Buttigieg for FAA shutdown
content:
Ari Emanuel has a lot on his plate as the CEO of TKO Group and Hollywood superagent. But he had plenty of time to make a statement about the FAA grounding all flights nationwide after a technological malfunction on Friday.

But in a post on social media, Emanuel had a strange target for his anger — former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg.

Buttigieg served in the role under President Joe Biden but hasn’t been in office since January 2025 when Donald Trump emerged victorious in the 2024 election and his administration took over. Sean Duffy has been in the role since then and has had his own fair share of controversies under his watch, including the chaos that developed over the weekend. At a press conference about the outage, Duffy’s performance was widely panned by people of all political stripes for his lack of leadership.

However, Emanuel saw it was Buttigieg’s fault for not installing enough modern upgrades during his time as secretary. Interestingly, he had nothing to say about the current administration’s role.

No one’s hands are clean here. However, Mr. Secretary Buttigieg, you had four years in the job and infrastructure money, yet made zero progress modernizing the FAA. You left a failing system in place. THANKS!

— Ari Emanuel (@AriEmanuel) November 13, 2026

“No one’s hands are clean here. However, Mr. Secretary Buttigieg, you had four years in the job and infrastructure money, yet made zero progress modernizing the FAA. You left a failing system in place. THANKS!” Emanuel wrote.

Emanuel’s comments are peculiar given his TKO company has been under fire for their travel policies and business with Saudi Arabia. WWE just held a show in Riyadh around various missile attacks on the city, and employees are starting to speak up about how the company does not care for them and only values profit and greed.

The criticism is also surprising because Emanuel has been a prominent supporter of Barack Obama and longtime Democratic advocate. Of course, his brother Rahm served as White House Chief of Staff under President Obama and also as a Democrat in the House of Representatives and as Mayor of Chicago.

However, in spite of his left-leaning political interests and longtime Democratic party support, Ari Emanuel’s agency represented Donald Trump during his time on The Apprentice. And when Trump was first elected president, Ari Emanuel was reportedly vetted for a potential role in his administration. Just last month in an interview with PBS, Emanuel said he still talks to Trump and values the conversations outside an “echo chamber.”

As chairman of TKO, Ari Emanuel is also head of what stands as arguably the most pro-Trump sports league on the planet in UFC. Trump regularly attends UFC shows and is routinely celebrated by Dana White and many fighters. The MAGAfication of UFC peaked with an event at Trump’s White House this summer and the sitting president even (jokingly?) suggested White become his new press secretary. The ties between WWE and Trump also run deep with the McMahon family longtime friends and partners. Donald Trump is in the WWE Hall of Fame and Linda McMahon serves on Trump’s cabinet.

Having said all of that, it is odd to see Ari Emanuel condemn someone who hasn’t been in the job as Secretary of Transportation for two years, especially as it sounds like something you’d hear from conservative media. Blaming the Biden admin for issues like rising inflation and gas prices was a failed tactic for Republicans before the blue tsumani on Election Day 2026. It speaks to there being something potentially personal between Emanuel and Buttigieg that goes beyond your garden variety politics. Or maybe the political leanings of TKO are starting to rub off on their CEO.

title: Padres Interested In Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez, Matthew Boyd
content:
The Padres have interest in free agent starters Freddy Peralta and Nick Martinez, according to ESPN’s Alden Gonzalez.  Matthew Boyd is another name of interest to the team, as per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune, though Acee notes that the Padres have “showed some level of interest in virtually every starting pitcher on the market….rather than list the starters whose representatives the Padres talked to, suffice it to say there is hardly a starting pitcher they are not considering.”

The rotation push is understandable given that Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Walker Buehler, Casey Mize, Robbie Ray, and Griffin Canning are all free agents.  This leaves San Diego with a current starting staff of Randy Vasquez, JP Sears, Joe Musgrove (who may be used in the bullpen), newly-signed swingman candidate Ryan Weiss, and maybe Yu Darvish, if the veteran still wants to continue his career.

Suffice it to say, the Padres need to fill at least four and maybe five rotation spots this winter, leaving the team searching every corner of the starting pitching market (and undoubtedly the trade market as well).  Peralta, Martinez, and Boyd represent a range of starters and potential price points for the Friars.  On our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, MLBTR projected Peralta for a five-year, $110MM contract, Martinez for two years and $42MM, and Boyd for a one-year, $13MM deal.

Peralta’s final price tag will be particularly interesting to gauge, as the right-hander struggled with the Mets before regaining his old form after a deadline trade to the Rays.  The possibility exists that a straight five-year, nine-figure commitment won’t be there for Peralta if teams are wary about his extended cold stretch in New York, which might present an opening for a creative executive like Padres president of baseball operations A.J. Preller.  The Padres’ past deals with the likes of King and Pivetta included opt-outs, so it could be that Peralta might be open to such an early off-ramp in order to re-enter the market on the strength of a stronger platform year.

Martinez is no stranger to these types of Padres contracts, as he signed two different deals with San Diego after returning to the majors from a four-year stint in Japan from 2018-21.  Martinez worked as both a starter and reliever over two seasons with the Padres, and 2026 marked the first time in his nine MLB seasons that the right-hander worked exclusively as a starter.  The result was a very solid season in Tampa Bay’s rotation, setting Martinez up for a multi-year deal even though he is already 36 years old.

Boyd is also entering his age-36 season, and he missed some time due to arthroscopic knee surgery in 2026.  The southpaw has a lengthy health history but (last year’s meniscus tear aside) he has been generally healthier over the past two seasons with the Cubs, delivering a 3.50 ERA over 306 1/3 innings.  Boyd projects as a third starter type at best, but that would be fine for the Padres if they can land some other frontline arms who are clearer candidates to start a playoff game.

After evaluating many options during the GM Meetings, Preller told Acee and other reporters that he’d be speaking this coming week with new owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones plus team CEO Erik Greupner to discuss the Padres’ spending capacity.  “Jose and Kwanza are open to having those conversations, open to what that means from a different dollar amount and different contract commitments, and hopefully we make some good decisions,” Preller said.

As Feliciano and Jones enter their first full season in charge of the club, Acee writes that the duo plan to spend at least as much on payroll as in 2026, and for San Diego to be at least a top-10 payroll club.  MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker calculates the Padres’ approximate $224MM payroll in 2026 as ninth in the league, with a luxury tax number of roughly $269.4MM that sat sixth among all teams.

Looking ahead to next year, San Diego has a little over $193MM on the books and a tax number of around $192.6MM, which allows Preller for some flexibility.  To some extent, Feliciano and Jones may feel compelled to increase spending out of sheer need, given the Padres’ needs in not just the rotation, but also in the bullpen and a couple of lineup holes.

Turning to the relief corps, Acee writes that the Padres had some interest in Evan Phillips before the right-hander signed a three-year, $35MM contract with the Braves.  The Friars saw plenty of Phillips during his six seasons with the Dodgers, and if nothing else, the Padres will be glad to see him out of the NL West — Phillips has a sparkling 1.19 ERA over 22 2/3 career innings against San Diego.

title: ‘College GameDay’ returns to Army-Navy Game for first time since 2023
content:
College GameDay is making its first appearance at the famed Army-Navy Game for the first time in multiple years.

The flagship ESPN college football program has had on and off appearances at the standalone contest over the years. The last time it made the visit was in 2023 when the game took place in Foxborough, Massachusetts.

This year the Army-Navy Game will be at Metlife Stadium in the Meadowlands for the 127th edition of the classic rivalry on December 12. With the expansion of the College Football Playoff, the game will move up a week next year and maintain its standalone date in 2027.

ESPN made the announcement of its latest visit on Saturday morning during the College GameDay live show in Boise State.

GameDay has come under scrutiny like never before with the outsized presence of Pat McAfee transforming the beloved institution and becoming the show’s centerpiece, whether fans like it or not. There’s also the backdrop of ESPN’s mega-contract with the SEC and the show being questioned for repeatedly returning to the same venues multiple times. Some of that criticism has extended to the content of the show, which has been severely lacking in anything substantive outside the SEC and Big Ten.

However, it seems like College GameDay has at least heard some of those criticisms and made a conscious effort to cast a wider net across college football in recent weeks. In fact, the show hasn’t visited an SEC school since all the way back on October 10 at Alabama. Recent stops have included BYU, Utah, and Boise State.

The Army-Navy Game has drawn some of its biggest viewership numbers ever over the past couple of years on CBS. You can certainly make the argument that College GameDay should make the trip every year. And whatever playoff implications may or may not be on the line, it’s a game that has always mattered a great deal to college football and American sports as a whole.

title: AL Central Notes: White Sox, Twins, Burg, Guardians
content:
The White Sox are focused on bolstering their rotation this winter, both with external additions and internal moves like moving Grant Taylor from the bullpen to a starting role.  Even with Taylor leaving the relief mix, however, GM Chris Getz downplayed the idea of prioritizing the bullpen when speaking with the Chicago Sun-Times’ James Fegan and other reporters.  Rather than invest heavily in relievers, the Sox could use any excess starters in bullpen roles, with perhaps a lower-cost veteran or two added later in the offseason for added depth.

Since the White Sox are so deep in infield prospects, it has been suggested that the club could trade from this depth to address other needs.  Getz didn’t rule this possibility out in the future, but it is “not something that I would say we’re entertaining right now.”  It’s a fair stance to take, as the Sox might not want to move any younger talent until they have a better idea of which of these infielders they view as true building blocks.  Despite Chicago’s unexpected AL Central title, the Sox aren’t going to pivot entirely away from their rebuilding plan, and the current infield grouping of Miguel Vargas, Colson Montgomery, Chase Meidroth, and Munetaka Murakami all contributed heavily to the playoff run.

More from around the AL Central…

  • The Twins have a significantly greater need in the bullpen than in the rotation, but could be taking somewhat of the same approach as the White Sox to the relief corps.  Minnesota could look to add to its rotation (probably more of a mid-rotation type) and then use at least one of the leftover starters to fill a hole in the bullpen, The Athletic’s Dan Hayes writes, since the Twins have traditionally never been eager about spending much money on relief pitching.  GM Jeremy Zoll acknowledged that his team would “need to be open-minded to” potential rotation adds, “knowing that it feels like an area of surplus but also want to be mindful of not eating into that too much since we know we’re going to need real depth to attack the season.”  Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley, and the returning Pablo Lopez line up as the projected top three in Minnesota’s rotation, with Dean Kremer, Zebby Matthews, Bailey Ober, Connor Prielipp, and Mick Abel all competing for the final two slots.
  • The Guardians are hiring Alex Burg as their new quality control coach, Justice delos Santos of the Bay Area News Group reports.  Burg has been on the Giants’ coaching staff for the last five seasons, working as a bullpen coach in 2022-23, the catching coach for the last three seasons, and he was also San Francisco’s Major League field coordinator this past year.  In between the end of his nine-year minor league career and the start of his tenure with the Giants, Burg also spent three years on the Rangers’ staff.

Aaron Rodgers shares heartfelt picture with Jordan Rodgers after family reconciliation
content:
After years of a public family feud, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers appears to have fully reconciled with his brother and ESPN analyst Jordan Rodgers.

The elder Rodgers has made headlines over the years for his complex relationships regarding his family and various love interests. The rift became public when younger brother Jordan appeared on Season 12 of The Bachelorette in 2016. It was revealed that Aaron Rodgers was no longer on speaking terms with his family, including his brother.

While it was thought that actress Olivia Munn and her relationship with Aaron Rodgers could have been at the center of the breakdown of the family dynamic, he insisted that there were deep-rooted issues in the Rodgers clan.

But earlier this year, things suddenly began to change. In July, Aaron Rodgers posted a picture of himself with his parents and other family members, signaling that the longstanding feud had come to an end and that there had been a reconciliation. However, Jordan Rodgers was absent from the photos.

But with Jordan Rodgers in Pittsburgh on Friday night with ESPN to call a college football game between the Pitt Panthers and Florida State Seminoles, Aaron Rodgers dropped by the broadcast booth to say hello. And the brothers posted a picture of their reunion to Instagram to signal to the world that all is now well with the family.

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by Aaron Rodgers (@aaronrodgers12)

“Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight @acrisurestadium. Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now @pitt_fb @mikemonaco_.” Rodgers’ caption of the photo read.

Say what you will about Aaron Rodgers, his personal beliefs, and some of the decisions he’s made over the years. But it’s great to see him fully reconciled with his family after so many years of pain and sadness, especially his brother. Jordan Rodgers has built a nice career as an ESPN college football analyst. Rodgers is flying high with the Pittsburgh Steelers and now happily married. He credited his wife this offseason with helping the healing process and move forward. And hopefully the Rodgers brothers can now enjoy each other’s company and make up for lost time.

title: Desmond Howard questions Heisman candidacy of Jeremiah Smith
content:
Jeremiah Smith may be the Heisman Trophy favorite at the moment, but the star wide receiver for the Ohio State Buckeyes is taking fire from both friends and enemies.

Smith somehow remains in the top spot in the Heisman rankings in spite of the disastrous nosedive of the Ohio State season and the pressure facing Ryan Day in Columbus. It all started spiraling after quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an injury against the Indiana Hoosiers. Day chose to go with true freshman Luke Fahey as the backup instead of five-star recruit Tavien St. Clair and the Buckeyes have lost consecutive games by double digits for the first time in years.

It was clear that Smith was visibly frustrated during OSU’s embarrassing home loss to Oregon. And he was controversially called a “petulant child” by beat writer Jeremy Birmingham. Now he’s receiving criticism from a place where you would more naturally suspect, a prominent Michigan alum.

ESPN College GameDay analyst Desmond Howard called out Jeremiah Smith on Friday for his lack of impact on the Buckeyes. Howard appeared on First Take and questioned the entirety of the Heisman field, saying that nobody has stood out yet for having a big moment in a big game. He would know that first-hand as his punt return touchdown against the Buckeyes in the biggest rivalry in the sport propelled his own campaign in 1991.

Desmond Howard on Jeremiah Smith

“When in the last two seasons has Jeremiah Smith been the difference in big games?”

Desmond says he hasn’t seen it yet.

We all know Jeremiah Smith is an incredible talent, but Desmond is questioning whether his impact in the biggest games matches the hype surrounding him.

The hype is generational. Desmond is asking where the generational moments are.

— Michigan Metal (@Metaleka_) November 13, 2026

“When you talk about Jeremiah, it’s more than just losing Julian Sayin. You’ve got to have those moments. In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith, the wide receiver at Ohio State, was the difference in a big game in the last two years. This season and last season. Give me that game. As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that makes me say ‘he was the guy,'” Howard said.

Desmond Howard hasn’t exactly been neutral in his commentary about Ohio State over the years as he routinely picks against the Buckeyes. That’s fine, it’s what rivalry is all about. In fact, it’s one of the reasons why Kirk Herbstreit isn’t as popular with Buckeye fans as Howard is with Wolverine fans. Herbstreit has gone to extreme lengths to project neutrality and criticized the Ohio State fanbase on multiple occasions.

But this commentary goes beyond rivalry trolling and makes you wonder what games Desmond Howard is watching. The two-year cutoff is convenient given Jeremiah Smith had 5 catches for 88 yards and a touchdown in a national championship game, including the game-clinching catch.

As for this season, before the Sayin injury, Smith put up spectacular numbers in Ohio State’s biggest games.

At #4 Texas, he put up 8 catches for 164 yards and a score before the team collapsed in the fourth quarter to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory.

Against #14 Iowa, he had 11 catches for 206 yards and a score.

Against #5 Indiana, he also led the Buckeyes with 4 catches for 68 yards and another touchdown.

What else is Jeremiah Smith supposed to do at this point? Even in last year’s playoff loss to the Miami Hurricanes he posted 157 yards and a touchdown. Against Oregon, he went nearly two full quarters without being targeted while the game got away from Ohio State. He can’t call the plays, throw, and catch.

There’s a lot of things that you can point to as going wrong in the Ohio State season, but Jeremiah Smith showing up in big games and continually proving himself to be one of the greatest receivers in the history of college football isn’t one of them.

KBO’s SSG Landers Sign Lyon Richardson
content:
The SSG Landers of the KBO League announced Thursday that right-hander Lyon Richardson was signed to a one-year deal.  Richardson will earn $900K in salary, plus he received a $100K signing bonus for putting pen to paper.

A second-round pick for the Reds in the 2018 draft, Richardson has appeared in parts of the last four MLB seasons, though the large majority of his big league work came in 2025.  Richardson has a 6.48 ERA, 17.2% strikeout rate, and 14.6% walk rate over 58 1/3 innings and 42 games in the Show, with 37 2/3 of those innings coming in 34 appearances with the 2025 Reds.

Cincinnati designated Richardson for assignment last offseason and then outrighted him off its 40-man roster, but selected Richardson again in May for what proved to be his final two MLB games with the Reds.  Richardson was then DFA’ed and outrighted again, and he opted for free agency and landed with the Brewers on a minor league deal.  This new beginning led to another DFA/outright cycle and a second minors contract with Milwaukee, and Richardson’s time in the organization resulted in 1 2/3 innings of big league work in one game.

Richardson is out of minor league options, and would’ve been limited to fielding only minors contracts this winter if he’d stayed focused on remaining in North America.  With the lockout looming, Richardson might not have found a new deal with an MLB team for months, so signing with the Landers gives him both added financial security and the ability to now focus solely on baseball.

While he has worked mostly as a reliever in the majors and minors over the last few years, Richardson will return to starting duties with the Landers.  Richardson’s career-long control problems remain an obstacle, but a solid showing in the KBO League could get him back onto the radar for MLB teams in a year’s time, and perhaps with a larger payday awaiting if he can re-establish his value as a starting pitcher.

title: Blue Jays Interested In Teruaki Sato
content:
At least seven teams have been publicly linked to Teruaki Sato’s market, and The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon reports that the Blue Jays also have interest in the Hanshin Tigers slugger.  The news comes as no surprise, given the Jays’ need for offense, their tendency to check in on virtually every free agent available, and the team’s increasing forays into the Japanese talent market.

Last winter’s signing of Kazuma Okamoto represents the high point of Toronto’s overtures to Japanese players, though Okamoto’s presence also creates a bit of an obstacle in regards to Sato, who is also a third baseman.  Sato also has experience as a corner outfielder and isn’t considered a premium defender at any of his positions, so he might well end up getting a good chunk of DH time in the majors.  The Blue Jays have vacancies to fill in both left field and DH, plus Sato could still get the odd turn at third base if Okamoto is given a DH day or an off-day.

Sato has been at least a productive hitter during all six of his NPB seasons, but his last two seasons in particular have been stellar, highlighted by a Triple Crown-winning campaign in 2026.  Sato delivered 39 homers, 106 RBI, and a .306/.383/.609 slash line over 614 PA for the Tigers last season, and he also went deep 40 times for the 2025 club.  If Sato can translate any of this power over to the majors, it would be a huge boost to a Blue Jays team that finished with a league-worst 152 home runs in 2026.

Despite all their offensive struggles last year, the Jays’ 19% strikeout rate was the second-lowest in baseball, topped only by the Rays.  Toronto has prioritized contact hitting and putting the ball in play, so this might make Sato less of a fit given how his NPB production has come along with a lot of strikeouts.  As Bannon notes, the Jays liked Okamoto last winter in part because he was known as a quality contact hitter in Japan, but Okamoto’s strikeout rate ballooned to 28.8% in his first year of MLB action.  In context, Sato had a 26.7 K% with the Tigers last year.

MLB Trade Rumors ranked Sato seventh on our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, and projected a five-year, $80MM deal for a player entering his age-28 season.  The price tag shouldn’t be much of an object for a Jays team that has paid the luxury tax in three of the last four seasons, and exceeded the maximum tax threshold in 2026.  The question is whether or not the Blue Jays would prefer to make another significant investment in a player without any MLB experience, or if the Jays would prefer to spend on a player with more of a proven track record.

Sato is one of many hitters reportedly on Toronto’s offseason radar thus far, as the team could feasibly look to address any position in the lineup except third base (Okamoto), starting catcher (Alejandro Kirk), and first base (Vladimir Guerrero Jr., coming off the worst season of his career).  Since pitching is also a need, the Blue Jays will surely want to check at least a couple of boxes off their lengthy offseason to-do list before the lockout.

title: Donte Whitner disgusted by Jameis Winston’s ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’ hard count
content:
Jameis Winston is a professional content creator despite his title of New York Giants backup quarterback. Some people can’t get enough of his cartoonish persona, while others see right through it.

Former NFL defensive back Donte Whitner has announced himself as a member of the latter group.

On Thursday night, the Giants lost a 24-21 heartbreaker to the visiting Washington Commanders. Late in the fourth quarter, Giants head coach John Harbaugh trotted out Winston to try to draw the Commanders offside on a fourth-and-1.

The Prime Video broadcast picked up Winston’s obnoxious cadence.

“Get ready! Get set! Hut 1, hut 2, hut 3!”

Alright, that’s performative, but not particularly memorable.

But then Winston started singing the 2000 Baha Men hit “Who Let The Dogs Out.”

If you listen to nothing else today, at least listen to Jameis Winston’s hard count here lmao https://t.co/F1nr26EN3W

— NFL (@NFL) November 13, 2026

Plenty of people thought it was hilarious, including Prime’s Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit, but Whitner didn’t crack a smile.

“I’d cut Jameis Winston this morning,” Whitner said on ESPN’s Get Up on Friday. “It was so unrealistic. You have 10 other guys other there, and guys on defense, busting their butt every week, and it’s very hard and difficult to win a game in the National Football League. So when you get up there—first and foremost, who ever says hut 1, hut 2, hut 3? That’s 1950s football!”

“And then when you go into ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’? Are you serious?” Whitner continued. “He’s clearly just trying to go viral on social media while they’re trying to win a football game. He’d get his pink slip this morning.”

Harry Douglas admitted to “crying laughing” in disbelief while watching Winston’s antics in his hotel room before Get Up host Mike Greenberg recentered the conversation on Whitner’s critique. Greenberg asked Douglas to weigh in on Winston seemingly “not taking seriously trying to get the other team to jump.”

“If anybody for the Washington Commanders would have jumped on ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’? If I’m [Washington head coach] Dan Quinn, I’m cutting their a**,” Douglas said.

Greenberg disclosed that everyone at Get Up laughed about it in the production meeting, except for Whitner. “I didn’t find it funny,” Whitner confirmed.

On Friday, reporters asked Harbaugh whether Winston’s colorful cadence bothered him.

“That ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’ thing, while it was, I think, probably fun on his part, so to speak, the way the cadence sounds, it was still an attempt to still draw them offsides,” Harbaugh said, per SNY.

“Does it bother me? No,” Harbaugh added. “I heard him do it in practice.”

The Giants briefly turned to Winston after Jaxson Dart underwent season-ending knee surgery in September. Winston’s short-lived stint as starting quarterback ended in Week 7, when the Giants opted for J.J. McCarthy. New York acquired McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28.

The Giants (5-3-1) will next host the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at MetLife Stadium on Nov. 22.

title: The Opener: Bauers, Ausmus, Kopech
content:
Former Padres owner Peter Seidler passed away at age 63 on this day in 2023.  Seidler was part of the Ron Fowler-led ownership group that bought the Padres in 2012, and then became club chairman in 2020 after buying out enough of Fowler’s stake of the team to become the majority shareholder.  In his three years of running the team, Seidler turned the Padres into one of the league’s biggest spenders in an all-out push to try and bring San Diego its first World Series title.  While the Padres only made it as far as the 2022 NLCS during Seidler’s brief tenure, Seidler became a beloved figure in baseball, and his legacy has carried forward as the team has remained in contention.

1. Bauers heads to Boston

The Red Sox made an early and somewhat unexpected splash in the free agent market yesterday, agreeing with Jake Bauers on a four-year, $58MM deal.  The plan is to have Bauers share the first base and DH duties with Willson Contreras, and with the designated hitter spot now essentially covered on a daily basis, it only increases the likelihood that odd men out Masataka Yoshida and Jarren Duran might not be back with the Sox in 2027.  With the November 20th non-tender deadline looming, Duran could simply be let go, given his projected $11.1MM salary.  Of the eight free agents who were issued qualifying offers, Bauers was perhaps the best candidate to accept the one-year, $23.15MM contract, so it seems likely that we won’t see anyone accepting the QO before Tuesday’s deadline.

2. Bagwell discusses Ausmus hiring

The Astros hired Brad Ausmus as their new manager earlier this week, and team senior advisor Jeff Bagwell provided some context on the decision in an interview with MLB.com’s Brian McTaggart.  Bagwell pointed to Ausmus’ varied resume on and off the field, and Ausmus’ experience as a catcher was of particular note.  “When you’re a catcher, you control so much with your team because you control your pitching staff,” Bagwell said.  “You cannot win without pitching.  We, for the last few years, have really worn our bullpen down and have gotten a lot of injuries.  I’m not saying it’s because of our coaching staff, but we have to have somebody that understands pitchers, and nobody does that better than catchers.”  While Ausmus and Bagwell are longtime friends dating back to their time as teammates in Houston, Bagwell dismissed the idea that he was “banging the table for Brad,” saying that owner Jim Crane and GM Randy Flores had to approve the hiring.  “Most people who get jobs in the game are friends with somebody.  That’s how it works.  How do you think you find people?  They just don’t show up.  You’ve got to find people, and generally, they’re acquaintances you have throughout the game,” Bagwell said.

3. Kopech set for showcase

Michael Kopech didn’t pitch in 2026, but the right-hander will throw for evaluators from multiple teams today, as reported by The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal, Will Sammon, and Katie Woo earlier this week.  A veteran of six MLB seasons, Kopech has found success as both a starter and a reliever, but was used only out of the bullpen in 2024-25 in the wake of a rough season in the White Sox rotation in 2023.  Injuries have been a major subplot of Kopech’s career, and shoulder and knee problems limited him to just 11 relief innings for the Dodgers in 2025.  The Giants and Yankees were linked to Kopech’s market last winter, but no deal was reached.  Kopech figures to have to settle for a minor league pact this winter, and if has solved his control problems and can stay healthy, he could offer plenty of upside to a team’s bullpen.

title: Mauricio Pochettino Leaves The USMNT For An Even Bigger Mess
content:
After an extended denouement to a doomed tenure, Manchester United finally set manager Michael Carrick loose on Thursday, hoping to put an end to the club's worst league start in 40 years. On Friday, the next era for England's most famous club began, sort of, as United announced that Mauricio Pochettino would be leaving the U.S. men's national team on Nov. 18 in order to become the new boss at Old Trafford.

Carrick's departure is no surprise, but Pochettino's arrival counts as a bit of a shock. Pochettino had famously come to international prominence first at Southampton and then in his five-season-plus stint at Tottenham Hotspur, which saw that club's evolution from an also-ran into, well, an also-ran that could actually fight with the big boys. Eventually, his tenure there grew stale and the lack of trophies forced a move, with Tottenham firing him in November of 2019. The Argentine then took a year off before signing on to succeed Thomas Tuchel at Paris Saint-Germain in early 2021; his first half-season there wasn't great, as he oversaw the only PSG squad to not win the Ligue 1 title this decade. He did go on to win the league in his first full season, but PSG let him go in the summer of 2022 anyway. A return to the Premier League with Chelsea followed in 2023, where he finished in sixth place in his only season at Stamford Bridge.

That brings us to September 2024, when Pochettino became manager of the USMNT ahead of the 2026 World Cup cycle. His appointment was a big deal, as he became the highest-paid and most accomplished manager in the country's history (Jurgen Klinsmann will quibble with the latter assessment, but whatever) in advance of a home(-ish) World Cup. Pochettino had a rocky start there, but eventually righted the ship enough to guide the USMNT to a Group D first-place finish and a Round of 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. An embarrassing loss to Belgium in the Round of 16 put a bit of a damper on the run, but overall, Pochettino did what he was hired to do: help the USMNT perform at the World Cup.

title: Would You Get Stoned With The Scythians?
content:
It's just like they told you it would happen in D.A.R.E.: You have been miraculously, tragically transported 2,800 years back in time, in the land that is now the Uyuk Valley of southern Siberia. The site will be eventually called Tunnug 1 by the archaeologists who excavate it in 2017. But that is the future, and this is the present, meaning 800 B.C. You have come to sit with the Scythians, nomads who roamed the Eurasian steppes on horseback. You have even glimpsed their warrior-king, whose long and stately braids make him seem like a pretty cool guy. Also, he's smoking. Suddenly the warrior-king glimpses you back, his reddish eyes glinting in the firelight. He leans over to you, whispers something inscrutable in an Eastern Iranic language, and extends in his grizzled hands an ancient joint, leaving you with only one question: Would you smoke that shit?

There are, to be certain, pros and cons. But one thing is clear, per a paper published recently in the journal Science: The Scythians were definitely using cannabis to get high. The analysis, led by Fabio-haired University of Bern archaeologist Gino Caspari, represents the earliest definitive evidence of humans consuming marijuana as a psychoactive drug, which was previously only traced back 2,500 years ago where Sogdian mourners once lit up in the ancient Jirzankal Cemetery in what is now western China.

It's only fitting that marijuana hails from one of the highest places in the world: the eastern Tibetan Plateau, also known as the Roof of the World. The plant evolved around 28 million years ago, and as early as 4,000 years ago Chinese farmers cultivated the plant for rope, clothing, and paper, per Science. But it is harder to tell when in the archaeological record ancient people first became gone off that loud. Wild weed, the ancestors of the domesticated kind, has only a little tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC, the plant's intoxicating compound. Some researchers confirmed this when they tried to smoke wild weed and felt nothing, also per Science. (It is unclear if these particular researchers are also the paper's authors, who described cannabis as an "illicit" substance.)

title: Horny Nvidia CEO No Longer CEO, Possibly Still Horny
content:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who is worth over $100 billion, resigned as CEO on Thursday morning, following an emergency board meeting prompted by several reports that he'd been having various affairs, most notably with someone U.S. officials believe was spying on behalf of the Chinese government.

Nvidia has an unorthodox corporate structure, built around Huang, which largely eschews traditional executive roles in favor of a large council of vice presidents who report directly to Huang, which makes the matter of his succession trickier to game out than it would be in other cases of a CEO doing sex stuff. He'll be succeeded on an interim basis by Colette Kress, formerly the CFO, whom Wired characterizes as one of the few people with a high-level grasp of the company's finances and ties to Wall Street.

A quick recap of how we got here: Nvidia is the single most important hardware technology company in the world, a chip designer that boosted its market cap to more than $4 trillion by making the must-have picks and shovels of the ongoing AI boom. As such, Nvidia is something like a shadow arm of the U.S. government, the latter of which is engaged in the stupidest-ever version of the space race with China over who can build the machine god first. Nvidia wants to sell its best stuff to Chinese companies because it doesn't really care who wins, as long as it makes money for investors, but the Trump administration won't allow it. Meanwhile, the tip-top Chinese AI companies have found ways to smuggle in the best Nvidia chips via third parties mostly based in Southeast Asia.

title: How I Succumbed To Reef Madness And Came To Love A Slowly Sinking Ship
content:
The SS United States finally sank in the Gulf of Mexico at around 10 p.m. ET Wedneday night. Not since the Minnow had a doomed vessel’s last tour run so far over schedule and still kept viewers engaged. Those who stuck with the 10-hour livestream were rewarded with an amazingly touching denouement. 

The ship had its day. The SS United States hit the seas in 1952, and at 990 feet long was about 100 feet longer than the Titanic, yet was able to hit speeds of more than 38 knots, still faster than any transatlantic ocean liner ever. But it was deemed obsolete and taken out of service way back in 1969, and spent the last 30 years docked in Philadelphia. Attempts to keep the SS US above water as a hotel or museum failed, and some folks in Okaloosa County, Florida, decided the liner was most valuable at the bottom of sea. The county floated a $10 million plan to turn the ship into an artificial reef and thereby enhance the Redneck Riviera’s reputation as a fishing and scuba diving destination. This entailed sinking the SS US about 22 miles off Fort Walton Beach during the very same week that the Edmund Fitzgerald hit bottom 51 years earlier.

title: ‘Mario Vargas Llosa: A Life’ Is Dishy And Definitive
content:
Mario Vargas Llosa: A Life might seem like a bland title for a biography, until it dawns on you exactly how much living the man did. He eloped with his aunt at 19, then humiliated her by writing a novel about it translated into more than 30 languages; divorced her for her much younger niece, his first cousin; and, after a scandalous 50-year marriage beset by separations, walked out one last time for the Spanish socialite and tabloid favorite Isabel Preysler, ex-wife of Julio Iglesias and mother of Enrique.

Arguably the world’s most famous Peruvian after Paddington, Vargas Llosa would have been president if not for the dark-horse populist Alberto Fujimori—father of the current president—who handily defeated Vargas Llosa’s platform of neoliberal shock economics in 1990. And in 2010, at age 74, he won the Nobel Prize in Literature, joining the pantheon alongside his lifelong frenemy Gabriel García Márquez, whom he famously punched in the face at a film premiere, for reasons that remain unclear. 

Thus, the page count of the new biography—the first since his death in 2025 and almost certainly the last word on the subject—clocking in at 812. Gerald Martin, a British critic who also wrote the definitive book on García Márquez, spent 25 years interviewing Vargas Llosa and those who knew him. The result is a monumental achievement: a synthesis of his subject's personal and political life with a surgical yet shockingly breezy analysis of the writing itself. And while it’s not always right to conflate fictional characters with their creator, Vargas Llosa is a special case, Martin argues: a novelist who peppered his work with confessions.

content:

Inter enter the new season as defending champions after securing their 21st Scudetto last season, while several of Italy’s leading clubs prepare to challenge for the crown under new leadership. AC Milan begin a new chapter under Rúben Amorim, Massimiliano Allegri takes charge of Napoli and Gennaro Gattuso begins his tenure at Lazio, while Gian Piero Gasperini enters his second season with Roma.
The season will feature 20 clubs competing across 38 rounds and 380 matches, with AC Milan, Napoli, Juventus, Roma and Lazio looking to challenge Inter for the Serie A title. The campaign will also see clubs battling for European qualification and to retain their place in Italy’s top flight.
Como enter the campaign following a landmark season in which they finished fourth, qualifying for the UEFA Champions League for the first time in the club’s history. They begin their new season away to Udinese on 22 August.
The new season also welcomes three promoted clubs: Venezia, Frosinone and Monza. Venezia return following promotion from Serie B, while Frosinone make their return to the top flight after a two-season absence. Monza secured their place in Serie A through the promotion play-offs.
The opening round brings several of the season’s key storylines into focus from the outset. Inter begin their title defence against Monza on Saturday, 22 August, while Napoli travel to Genoa for Allegri’s first Serie A appearance with his new club. The action continues Sunday, 23 August, as Frosinone mark their return to the top flight against Juventus, while Amorim faces his first Serie A test with AC Milan away to Torino. The round’s headline fixtures conclude on Monday, 24 August, when Roma face Fiorentina.

title: New York Knicks star OG Anunoby wins NBA championship in Skechers – a historic first
content:
History was made at the Frost Bank Center — and Skechers was right there on the court for every step of it.
OG Anunoby has been crowned an NBA Champion, becoming the first player in history to win an NBA title wearing Skechers Basketball footwear. For a brand that launched its basketball division just three years ago, it marks a defining moment.
Fresh off his iconic game-winning tip-in in Game 4, OG delivered another standout performance in the title-clinching Game 5, finishing with 28 points, five rebounds and two blocks while providing the two-way impact that helped power the Knicks to the championship.
From timely three-pointers to key defensive stops, Anunoby was one of the NBA Finals’ most influential performers throughout the series — and he did it all in Skechers. In true OG fashion, he even rotated through three pairs of Skechers during Game 5 alone: opening the game in a black colourway SKX Nexus, transitioning into the SKX Nexus “NYC Blue” PE, and closing out the championship in a yellow colourway SKX Nexus — a fitting exclamation point on a historic night.
        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SKECHERS (@skechers)

Throughout the playoffs and Finals, OG captivated fans not only with his performances, but also with the Skechers Player Exclusive styles he wore on court — several of which went viral:
SKX Nexus “Euro” PE
This style led to a now-legendary exchange and gifting moment with Knicks fan and Skechers ambassador Martha Stewart.
SKX Reign “Foreman” PE
Debuted during warmups ahead of Game 3 of the Finals as a nod to his repeated Defensive Player of the Game honours.
SKX Nexus “NYC Blue” PE
This bold blue-and-orange colourway, worn during his iconic Game 4 performance, paid tribute to the Knicks’ remarkable playoff run and the fans who made it possible.
        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SKECHERS (@skechers)

On court, OG rotated between two high-performance Skechers Basketball models that reflect his dynamic and versatile game:
• The SKX Nexus™ – a low-top performance shoe built for speed, stability and responsive comfort.
• The SKX Reign™ – designed for elevation and elite traction to keep OG locked in at both ends of the floor.
The milestone extends beyond basketball. OG is now a two-time NBA Champion, having first won a title with the Toronto Raptors in 2019, when he became the first British-born player to win an NBA championship.
Skechers is the world’s third-largest footwear brand and has rapidly assembled one of basketball’s most exciting athlete rosters, including Joel Embiid, Julius Randle, Isaiah Hartenstein, Norman Powell and WNBA stars Jackie Young, Rickea Jackson and Kiki Iriafen, alongside elite athletes across running, golf, football, pickleball and cricket.

title: SPIA celebrates the Middle East’s sports industry stars in gala evening in Abu Dhabi
content:
The 13th edition of the Sports Industry Awards (SPIA) returned to Abu Dhabi for a second successive year to celebrate the region’s finest in a special evening. 
Hosted by Sport36X and Interact as part of Sport Industry Series, Wednesday’s gala event at the Space42 Arena welcomed over 500 guests to the capital’s Space42 Arena to honour the individuals, organizations, venues and initiatives that are shaping the sports industry across the Middle East.
The awards night was held in a strategic partnership with the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi, with further support being extended by the Abu Dhabi Sports Council (ADSC). Jetour Elite Group Holding served as the Title Sponsor of the event, while Motus One came on board as the Gold Sponsor. MRamez Events and Spinneys were the Silver and Bronze sponsors respectively, with The Athletic making their debut as the media partners.
Winners across 26 different categories were selected by an independent panel of judges composed of industry stalwarts, chosen for their expertise in the Middle East sports industry. DP World Tour Championship, the 3rd Asian Youth Games Bahrain 2025, ADNOC Abu Dhabi Marathon and the ADEK All-Stars program were some of the big winners on the night.

The evening began with speeches from Bassam Nawfal, Managing Director of Sport360X and Sally Corander, Founder and CEO of Interact. H.E, Saeed Al Fazari, Strategic Affairs Executive Director of the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi then addressed the gathering to highlight the Emirate’s unwavering commitment to promote sport in the region.
“Over thirteen editions, SPIA has grown into far more than an awards ceremony. It has become the platform that brings this industry together. It recognises excellence. It sets the benchmark for what the very best looks like in sport across the Middle East,” Bassam said in his opening address.

“Earlier this year, our region went through a period that tested us. It affected all of us in different ways, and it reached every corner of our lives – our families, our communities and our industry. But, what stands out today is not the challenge. It is the response.

“The resilience of the UAE. Of Abu Dhabi. And, of the people in this room. Welcoming so many illustrious guests to Space42 Arena is a testament to the passion and momentum behind the Middle East’s sports industry.

“From outstanding campaigns to world-class facilities, the calibre of this year’s winners was truly inspiring. We’re also grateful to all our partners and sponsors whose support made this latest celebration possible.”
The different winners were selected after an extensive process of vetting more than hundred nominees by an esteemed panel of industry titans from across the region. 

These included: H.H. Princess Nouf Al Saud (General Manager – Marketing, Ministry of Sport Saudi Arabia), H.H. Ali Abdulrahman Al Ali (CEO, Dubai Racing Club), Richard Scudamore (Former Executive Chairman & CEO, Premier League), Fiona Jordan (Chief Brand Officer, Whisper), Mo Harb (Head of Partnerships, Tik Tok MENA), Melissa Moncada (CEO & Founder, Aurora Group), Danny Townsend (CEO, SURJ Sports Investment), Tom Foley (CEO, Go Sport), Shaima Alhusseini (Saudi Sports for all Federation, Managing Director), Sarah Swanson (Chief Brand Officer, WTA Ventures), Rob Pilgrim (Head of Sports EMEA, META), Jamie Dean (Executive Director – Sports, MODON), Simon Morris (Vice President, Marketing, International, Adobe), Karim Younes (Partner and COO, Entergame Sports Marketing), and Nick Pinder (Vice President of Sponsorships and Partnerships, International Cricket Council).

The DP World Tour Championship walked away with the coveted ‘Major Global Sports Event of the Year’ award while Elevate took home the ‘Best Agency of the Year’ trophy. The 3rd Asian Youth Games Bahrain 2025 clinched two awards on the night in the form of ‘Best Use of Social Media in Sport’ and ‘Athlete Wellbeing and Support Programme.’

The Yas Marina Circuit won the ‘Best Venue of the Year’ trophy while the ADNOC Abu Dhabi Marathon was the selection for ‘Best Fan Engagement in Sports.’ The ‘Amateur Sports Team/Club of the Year’ award was given to Banaat FC, while Desert Vipers were recognised for their ‘Excellence in Sustainability.’

The NBA Abu Dhabi games presented by ADQ won big by bagging the prestigious ‘Campaign of the Year’ award.

Two special recognition awards were also presented on the night. H.E. Ghanim Mubarak Al Hajeri was recognised as the ‘’Visionary Leader in Middle East Sport ’ while Cherie Pridham was presented with the ‘Female Leader in the Middle East’ recognition.

A highlight of the night was the interactive quiz of regional sports presented by Kahoot, with the attendees competing for lucrative prizes.

title: XX | HER EDITION launches women focused fitness competition as global events return to Dubai
content:
As the global events industry regains momentum following a period of uncertainty, a new fitness competition is launching in Dubai, one that shifts the focus away from elite performance and toward personal progress and participation.
XX | HER EDITION, a Dubai-born female fitness event, has been created specifically for women who are new to functional fitness or returning after time away. In an industry traditionally dominated by elite athletes and high-performance competition, XX is designed to make fitness more accessible, prioritising participation and community, while making competition more approachable.
Taking place on May 14, in partnership with GMG, the debut event will welcome 160 women to take part in a 30-minute functional fitness challenge completed in pairs. The format is designed to offer women the opportunity to experience the energy of competition in a uniquely supportive and inclusive environment.
The event brings together leading home-grown concepts and international brands from GMG’s portfolio – including Geant, Sun & Sand Sports and Supercare – alongside brands such as Built For Athletes and Science in Sport. All aligning with a shared vision to support women’s health, fitness, and wellbeing at a grassroots level. Hosting the event will be Rich Hayes, well-known podcast host and radio DJ, bringing his signature energy to the competition floor.
Behind XX | HER EDITION is Hannah Hall, CEO of Grassports and a seasoned event designer with over 16 years of experience delivering major sporting events across the UAE. Her portfolio includes industry-leading projects such as the DP World ILT20, Spinneys Dubai 92 Cycle Challenge, Arabian Warrior, and Women’s Epic Arabia.
Hannah Hall comments, “Sports and fitness events need a shake-up. There has been too much focus on elite performance for too long. XX | HER EDITION is about creating a platform for everyday women, those starting out, returning, or simply looking for a new challenge in a supportive environment. Participation should be celebrated just as much as performance.”
She continues,“We’re also seeing a shift in how brands want to engage with communities. Our partners understand that investing in real people, real journeys, and accessible fitness experiences has far greater long-term impact.”
Florian Hüthmair, President – Everyday Goods, said: “We aim to be an enabler for community events by bringing active living-inspired experiences to our customers. Through partnerships like XX | HER EDITION, we’re helping create welcoming spaces where women can show up, try something new, and feel supported—whether they’re just starting out or returning to fitness. Our objective is simple: to bring people together through movement and create environments where communities can connect, grow, and thrive.”
He continues: “At Géant we will continue to create in-store experiences for families and beyond, becoming the everyday premium food retail space where quality is daily and shopping is exciting.
“Our strategy revolves around food culture, music & art, and sports & active living. Our objective is to make Géant a true community hub—bringing people together through curated experiences, supporting healthier everyday choices, and creating a space where families and communities can connect, discover, and thrive.”
Following its launch, XX | HER EDITION will expand into a four-event series, including indoor summer editions and a trail-based event planned for winter 2026, continuing to grow its inclusive fitness community across the region.
With its focus on accessibility, empowerment, and community, XX | HER EDITION is set to introduce a more inclusive and inspiring approach to fitness competition for women in the UAE.

title: Dubai Sports Council launches Dubai Open Volleyball Academies Championship next Saturday
content:
DUBAI: The Dubai Sports Council announced the organisation of the ‘Dubai Open Volleyball Academies Championship’, the first of its kind in the region, that is scheduled to kick off on April 25 (Saturday), with the participation of 70 teams representing 25 academies and clubs from across the UAE. The championship is being held in cooperation with UAE Volleyball federation and Sports Mania and will continue until June 13, 2026.
The championship includes five age categories for males and females (under 10, 12, 14, 16, and 19 years old), and more than 250 matches are scheduled to be held at the Shabab Al Ahli Club indoor courts and the Al Safa Sports Hall in the Jumeirah area.
The Dubai Sports Council and the organising committee held a technical meeting with coaches and directors of participating academies. During the meeting, the technical and organisational regulations were reviewed, the match schedule was approved, and all participant inquiries were addressed.

Ali Omar Al Baloushi, Director of Sports Development at the Dubai Sports Council, emphasized that the Council prioritises talent discovery and development, stating: “We are working to build an integrated system to attract and nurture promising players across various sports. Launching this tournament reflects our commitment to providing a truly competitive environment that gives young athletes the opportunity to demonstrate their abilities and refine their skills by increasing the number of matches according to international standards.”
Al Baloushi added: “This tournament is part of the Council’s strategy to develop talent within Dubai clubs and enhance cooperation with the private sector to become an active partner in developing the sports sector by organising events that have a direct impact on youth development programmes.”

He also explained that the tournament complements a comprehensive strategic programme and joins the Dubai Open series of tournaments in football, basketball, handball, tennis, gymnastics, badminton and padel.
Tariq Abboud, Managing Director of Sports Mania, hailed the collaboration with the Dubai Sports Council, saying: “We are honoured to organise this tournament, which brings together government and private academies and clubs from across the country to compete in official matches that enhance the development of emerging talent.”
Abboud praised the high turnout and the keenness of coaches and team managers to attend the technical meeting, reflecting their strong enthusiasm for participating.
The participating clubs include Al Wasl, Shabab Al Ahli, Al Nasr, Hatta, and Al Dhaid, along with the academies of Wildcats, UIG Sports, FDR, Centrix, Centrline, One Dela Cruz, Next Gen, Hec Volleyball, Speed Sports, Spikers Abu Dhabi, Al Mawakeb, Abu Dhabi Volleyball Clinic, ATPV Com, Olympic Stars, and Esperia.

title: TCL brings Olympic-level performance home with next-generation QD-Mini LED TVs
content:
As the Winter Olympics once again showcased the speed, precision and intensity of elite sport, TCL used the global moment to reinforce a simple message for viewers at home: performance should not stop at the arena.
As a Worldwide Olympic Partner, the brand has been aligning itself with the values of excellence and innovation that define the Games. More importantly for consumers, that partnership is reflected in the technology TCL is putting into living rooms across the UAE.
At the centre of TCL’s offering is its QD-Mini LED TV lineup, a category where the company holds the position of Global No.1 Mini LED TV Brand, Global No.1 Ultra-Large Screen TV Brand and Global No.1 Google TV Brand, according to 2024 Omdia shipment data. For sports fans, those credentials translate into tangible viewing advantages rather than marketing claims.
Winter sports are among the most demanding types of content for any television. Bright white snow, rapid camera pans, high-speed motion and fine details all test a screen’s ability to handle contrast, clarity and brightness simultaneously.

TCL’s QD-Mini LED technology addresses this through ultra-precise backlight control, allowing the screen to manage light with far greater accuracy. The result is deeper blacks, brighter highlights and more defined details, even during fast transitions.
The flagship 115-inch X955 represents the most immersive expression of that technology. Designed as a stadium-scale display for the home, it combines exceptional brightness with refined contrast and expansive screen real estate.
When watching downhill skiing, figure skating or ice hockey, the scale alone transforms the experience, making viewers feel closer to the action. Subtle movements, such as the spray of ice during a sharp turn or the tracking of a puck across the rink, become clearer and more impactful.
For consumers who want high-performance sports viewing in slightly smaller formats, TCL’s 98-inch and 85-inch X11K models deliver strong brightness levels and advanced motion clarity that are particularly suited to fast-paced content. The 75-inch and 65-inch C8K series offer premium QD-Mini LED performance in more versatile sizes, balancing vivid color reproduction with smooth motion handling.
Across the lineup, the emphasis remains consistent: sharper detail, controlled light precision and immersive scale.

Motion clarity is especially critical when following live sport. Blurring during quick pans or high-speed sequences can reduce the sense of realism. TCL’s processing and backlight precision work together to maintain stability and smoothness, ensuring that split-second moments remain crisp.
For viewers in the UAE who regularly gather for major tournaments and international competitions, this level of clarity enhances not just individual enjoyment but shared viewing experiences as well.
While the display technology is the primary focus for sports fans, TCL’s broader home ecosystem also addresses another key regional consideration: climate. In a country where high temperatures are part of daily life, comfort is essential to any entertainment setup.
TCL’s VoxIN JetMax and SaveIN AI Invertor air-conditioning systems are engineered for fast cooling, intelligent temperature adaptation and energy-efficient performance in high heat and humidity.
JetMax is designed to deliver rapid temperature adjustment when returning home from the outdoors, while SaveIN AI Invertor optimizes energy consumption and maintains air quality to ensure consistent comfort.
Together, TCL’s large-format QD-Mini LED TVs and intelligent cooling solutions reflect a performance-led approach that mirrors the spirit of the Olympic Games. The same principles that define elite winter athletes – precision, endurance and control – are applied to how images are displayed and how environments are cooled.

For consumers, this means sharper sports visuals, immersive large-screen viewing and reliable comfort during long match days.
TCL’s recent Winter Olympics activation at Dubai Ice Rink provided visitors with an opportunity to experience these technologies firsthand. However, the real impact extends beyond the event itself.
The focus remains on delivering high-performance viewing solutions that elevate how sport is experienced at home, long after the final medal has been awarded.
As global competitions continue to unite audiences, the demand for clearer motion, brighter displays and larger screens will only grow. With its QD-Mini LED leadership and climate-ready cooling solutions, TCL is positioning itself as a premium technology partner for sports fans in the UAE who want every moment of the action to feel sharper, larger and closer to reality.
